eruvin/6.question: Is taking on the stringencies of two teachers who disagree an act of caution, or a way of following neither of them?

eruvin/9.question: Does passing a ruling on to students prove that a teacher accepts it, when declining to pass it on proves nothing either way?

eruvin/11.question: If Rav Sheshet hides the teaching that refutes him instead of changing his ruling, what is a ruling worth once the one who gave it knows the proof against it?

eruvin/12.question: If the smallest excess of length over width turns a courtyard into an alleyway, is a place defined by its shape or by how the people in it live?

eruvin/13.question: If words written for no one in particular become hers at the moment they are dissolved, what makes a document belong to a person: the writing of it or the use made of it?

eruvin/17.question: Once danger to the eyes is given as the reason washing after the meal still holds, what makes harm to a soldier's body a claim that cannot be waived while another man's firewood and the tithes owed on his produce can be?

eruvin/21.question: The boards bend Shabbat so a traveler can drink, while Akiva would rather go thirsty than eat with unwashed hands, so when does a rule the Sages added stop serving the person it was made for?

eruvin/22.question: If Joshua's allotment is what keeps the rough paths of Beit Gilgul out of the public domain, does a place become public from the crowds who cross it or from who was given the ground?

eruvin/24.question: If replacing a fence one cubit at a time makes it a new fence, is a thing made new by having its parts replaced, or by its owner wanting a different rule to apply to it?

eruvin/26.question: Does a student's duty to enforce his teacher's ruling still hold when the student can defeat that ruling with an argument of his own?

eruvin/29.question: If the beer measure is fixed by what people actually make a meal of, why does the Persians' habit of eating roasted meat without bread not settle that meat is a meal?

eruvin/30.question: When a measure is fitted to one particular body rather than to the average, is that only because nothing else is physically possible, as with the giant's doorway, or because what a person actually needs was always the point?

eruvin/31.question: Once the page says the priest would be glad to still have that food the next morning, can a commanded act ever be free of benefit while the person still wants the thing it uses?

eruvin/32.question: If the trust in each case rests on a court known to act promptly, what would make an ordinary messenger's errand worth relying on at all?

eruvin/34.question: If the food counts when the key is lost in a city but not when it is lost in a field, is a person's place for the day fixed by what he did before Shabbat or by chance after it?

eruvin/35.question: If Rabbi Meir presumes a man alive until it is known he died, why does contradictory testimony about the teruma leave no room for the same presumption that it was pure until known impure?

eruvin/36.question: If a presumed state is good enough to let a doubtful loaf serve as an eiruv, why can it not also stand in for food a person could actually have eaten before dark?

eruvin/37.question: If the objection is only that the flask might burst before he separates anything, does the wine become permitted to drink by what the man intends now, or only by what actually happens later?

eruvin/38.question: If nobody can settle whether a Festival and the Shabbat beside it are one sanctity or two, is the man who is both donkey driver and camel driver keeping the law, or only keeping the doubt?

eruvin/39.question: Can a day be kept as fully sacred in what it forbids and counted as an ordinary weekday in what it permits, or does eating the deer hollow one of the two days out?

eruvin/40.question: If Rav Yehuda can report that Rav and Shmuel limited the blessing to the three pilgrim Festivals and still say it over a gourd, why does watching Rav Ḥisda take up his cup decide what the reported tradition did not?

eruvin/41.question: If what settles the argument is how much hunger the body actually feels, is a fast a duty owed at fixed hours or a hardship measured person by person?

eruvin/46.question: If a single lenient opinion normally loses to the many, what changes under pressure that makes Rabbi Elazar worth relying on after all?

eruvin/47.question: If the rams are held in place only so that nobody comes to mishandle a Jew's goods, why does the restriction land on the gentile's animals rather than on the people who might err?

eruvin/50.question: Why should a herder's miscount be able to make animals holy when his deliberate choice of the same three could not?

eruvin/51.question: If the distance a person may walk on Shabbat is fixed by the distance an unwitting killer may stray from the city sheltering him, does the shared wording make the two boundaries about the same thing?

eruvin/52.question: If one step down the road can count as leaving, what is it about walking rather than deciding to go that changes where a person belongs on Shabbat?

eruvin/54.question: If Rabbi Perida receives both the added years and the share for his generation, was he ever really being asked to give anything up, or only to say out loud what he wanted?

eruvin/56.question: If those twelve hundred extra cubits at the corner exist only because a square was drawn around a round town, what makes the ground inside the square any nearer to home?

eruvin/61.question: If the ruling was issued to keep drunken men from beating their neighbors, why do Rav Safra and Rav Dimi bar \u1e24inana still work to make it come out right as ordinary measurement?

eruvin/63.question: If a teacher's honor gives way when someone else is breaking a prohibition in public, why does it not give way for Aaron's sons, who carried the fire because they read the verse as commanding it?

eruvin/65.question: If a mind too unsettled to pray is still clear enough to sell property or be sentenced to death, does prayer ask more of a person than anything else, or simply matter less?

eruvin/68.question: When no neighbor has actually asked for a piece, why should a share stop counting as shared just because Abaye could not have given it up if someone did?

eruvin/73.question: If taking a food allowance from a father leaves each brother a separate household, why should taking an allowance from a husband make a wife no household at all?

eruvin/74.question: If a person's residence is set by where he sleeps rather than where he eats his bread, what is it about sleeping somewhere that makes it the place he belongs to?

eruvin/81.question: If the rule stands even where no neighbor has anything to resent, why is a loaf that merely looks whole enough, and is the rule then about what was actually given or about what can be seen?

eruvin/82.question: If saying nothing counts as agreeing to another person's arrangement while quietly putting out your own food the other way counts as refusing it, is consent something a person gives or something others read off what she does?

eruvin/83.question: If a leftover of seven-twentieths of an egg is small enough to ignore, why is a gap of several eggs too large to be called a third?

eruvin/86.question: If the same hanging sheet counts as a wall over water but not over dry land, is a partition judged by what it actually blocks or by how serious the prohibition is?

eruvin/87.question: If the folded-down floor counts as a wall only where banks and towns already make the water look enclosed, is the imagined wall permitting the act or just restating how the place already looks?

eruvin/89.question: If Rav Yosef says he remembers it now but the ruling he recalls differs from the one Abaye heard him give, what makes his corrected version, rather than his student's memory, the teaching in Shmuel's name?

eruvin/93.question: If the strip beside the fence may not be sown only because no one can work it and its owner has renounced it, is a wall ever what changes the law, or only what people can do with the ground?

eruvin/95.question: If a man straps on a pair only to get them home safely and still counts as having done the commandment, can an act be obedience when the person doing it meant something else?

eruvin/96.question: If the woman carrying found phylacteries counts as proof only because Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda deny women any optional performance elsewhere, is the evidence her practice or their opinions about other cases?

eruvin/100.question: If climbing a bare dry tree breaks no rule, can Rav's fence around it in Apsetaya make the act a real transgression there, or only make the people of that town more careful?

eruvin/101.question: If a hinge that rotted away long ago counts as much as a hinge that still works, is the plank judged by what it is now or by what it once was?

eruvin/104.question: When a rule is set aside because the reason behind it is absent, and a different misuse later turns up, is it the old rule that comes back or a new one that Ameimar made himself?

pesachim/2.question: If the Gemara has already twice concluded that or means evening, what is it still looking for when it goes on testing verses?

pesachim/3.question: If the Torah itself drops delicate wording the moment it costs extra letters, why is one tired student's word for a pig enough for Rav to stop speaking with him?

pesachim/5.question: If the reading of "the first day" is surrendered and a different verse supplies the deadline, was the deadline ever really at risk, or does a rule hold steady while its proofs are traded in and out?

pesachim/6.question: Can a declaration made hours in advance settle what a person will want later, once the fine cake is in his hand?

pesachim/8.question: If the merit of the search guards a person only until he finishes it, and cannot be relied on where danger is common anyway, what is the promise of safety worth?

pesachim/9.question: When nobody saw which mouse entered which house, is assuming that the leaven went into the unsearched house a claim about what actually happened, or only a way of keeping the searched house permitted?

pesachim/12.question: If witnesses are careful about the hour and ordinary people are not, why do the Sages forbid leaven an hour early to protect the careless, while a court may execute a man on testimony that could be wrong by two hours?

pesachim/14.question: If the added impurity exists only because the Sages decreed it, is that a real loss to the meat, or nothing at all?

pesachim/16.question: If something can be impure in itself and still leave clean everything it touches, what does calling it impure amount to?

pesachim/18.question: If Rabbi Yosei passes on Rabbi Akiva's reading of the verse without accepting it, whose ruling is it when someone later relies on it?

pesachim/22.question: If Shimon HaAmmassoni was rewarded for abandoning his method, and Rabbi Akiva then expounded the very verse that stopped him, can a way of reading be wrong in one person's hands and right in another's?

pesachim/23.question: If the verse has to say that the harvest is still "yours", what does owning a thing amount to when you are the one person who may not eat it?

pesachim/24.question: If the reach of a ban depends on whether a verse happened to mention eating, does the wrong lie in the forbidden thing itself or in the wording that forbids it?

pesachim/28.question: If bread thrown whole into a river will dissolve anyway, is it destroyed once nobody can get it back, or only when nothing of it is left?

pesachim/29.question: Is the consecrated loaf worth something during the week it cannot be used, on the strength of what it will be worth later, or worth nothing until that day comes?

pesachim/30.question: If Shmuel thought his ruling was right, does respect for Rav's standing in his own town justify withholding it, and why should unfair prices be the thing that changes his mind?

pesachim/32.question: If, as Abaye says, the man gained nothing for the priest beyond produce that sells more easily, is being easy to sell a real part of what something is worth, or something extra the priest was never owed?

pesachim/34.question: If a rule was made because something might have gone wrong unseen, does proof that nothing went wrong end the rule, or has the rule by then become its own reason?

pesachim/35.question: If Rav Idi bar Avin's answer rests only on what fruit juice does to dough, does Rav Pappa's link between what counts as matza and what counts as forbidden leaven survive at all?

pesachim/39.question: If the test for maror is simply the taste of bitter herbs, what does it mean that the best maror is chosen for the story its bitterness tells rather than for how bitter it is?

pesachim/41.question: If the man at the hot springs broke no prohibition and only left the roasting undone, does failing to do what was commanded count as a wrong in the same way as doing what was forbidden?

pesachim/43.question: If women's obligation to eat matza comes only from their being forbidden leaven, is that obligation the same as one the verse states outright?

pesachim/49.question: If the first betrothal feast counts as a commandment and a second one does not, what turns a meal into an obligation rather than something a person simply wanted?

pesachim/50.question: If a person should perform the commandments even for ulterior motives, why fast so that scribes lose the pay that keeps them writing?

pesachim/51.question: If Abaye holds that Rabba bar bar Ḥana was entitled to eat that fat, why does hiding it drop two scholars to the level of people who cannot be told a leniency?

pesachim/52.question: When two reports of the same teacher's ruling contradict each other, is choosing the more careful reporter any different from choosing the answer you were hoping for?

pesachim/56.question: If a complaint from heretics was enough to turn a whispered line into a loud one, what became of the original doubt about whether the line belongs in the prayer at all?

pesachim/57.question: If consecrating property to Heaven was the only way owners could stop strong men from seizing it, why does the same move count against the people of Jericho when they did it with their sycamore trunks?

pesachim/58.question: If the only reason for the later hour disappears on Shabbat, should the hour go with it, or does keeping every day alike matter more than the reason behind the hour?

pesachim/59.question: Once the rule that all offerings finish before the afternoon lamb can be stretched so one leper may eat that night, is trusting the priests to be careful a real safeguard, or just a way to leave the rule looking intact?

pesachim/60.question: If Rava explains the difference by saying the registered eaters can change at any moment, is a status that only a spoken statement can undo really more settled than one other people's choices can undo?

pesachim/63.question: If a man can break this rule because of bread he does not own and never sees, kept far from the courtyard, what exactly is he answerable for?

pesachim/64.question: Can an arrangement be called safe when its safety depends on a miracle, given that on one Passover a man was crushed anyway?

pesachim/66.question: If the people arrived at the right practice on their own, why does it count as law only once Hillel recognizes it as what his teachers taught him?

pesachim/69.question: Was Akiva's silence about his teacher's forgetting respect, when saying it plainly might have spared him the curse?

pesachim/70.question: Can the law decide what a stranger did with his cleaver by counting the uncertainties he faced, when he never said a word about it?

pesachim/73.question: If even an animal slaughtered for idolatry counts as improved, because nobody can now eat a limb torn from it while alive, what act would ever be purely destructive?

pesachim/74.question: If each case brought to show that meat releases the blood it absorbed is explained away as special, what is Rabba's lenient ruling still resting on?

pesachim/75.question: If the word fire must mean a visible flame in one verse and a glowing coal in another, is the page finding out what fire is or deciding it verse by verse?

pesachim/76.question: When two sages disagree about whether a smell transfers anything at all, is the lenient view something Levi may act on at the Exilarch's table, or something he should have kept as his own opinion?

pesachim/77.question: If fire on the altar counts as consuming the meat, is an offering complete when it has been used up, or only when someone actually eats it?

pesachim/78.question: If the obligation is completed by the blood, why must the person it was slaughtered for still be someone capable of eating meat he will never eat?

pesachim/79.question: If the second Pesaḥ exists so that people blocked from the first can still bring the lamb, what justifies leaving half the community with no lamb at all?

pesachim/83.question: Why should a lamb's brief stretch of fitness still forbid breaking its bones once no one is allowed to eat it?

pesachim/87.question: If Hosea only learns why God stays attached to Israel by being handed a wife and children he cannot bear to send away, is an attachment arranged as a lesson still his own?

pesachim/90.question: Once a verse defers even a man who would have been pure by nightfall, what is left of the idea that a person is measured by what he will be by evening rather than by what he is now?

pesachim/92.question: The page lists which decrees held and which gave way but never says why; if the same cutting off hangs over both men, what makes one decree worth keeping?

pesachim/93.question: If bringing the lamb a month late cancels the punishment for deliberately skipping the first Pesach, in what sense was the first date required at all?

pesachim/95.question: If the later offering copies the lamb but not the festival day, with no leaven cleared out and no singing at the meal, is it the same festival kept late or a different obligation wearing its clothes?

pesachim/97.question: If an animal that goes missing at an hour when it could not be sacrificed was never lost at all, is being lost a fact about the animal or only about the time of day?

pesachim/98.question: Why must a lamb never be left ownerless even for an instant, when the same people end up registered for it either way?

pesachim/100.question: If Rabban Shimon stopped short only because students were watching, was the rule settled by the argument or by the audience?

pesachim/102.question: Once the page allows any number of blessings over one cup so long as they share a subject, why does Grace after Meals, said over that very cup of wine, count as a foreign matter?

pesachim/103.question: If deciding you are finished drinking cancels the first blessing while reciting kiddush over the same cup does not, is a blessing covering the wine or the drinker's intention?

pesachim/104.question: If the list only reaches seven because the line about priests, Levites and Israelites is counted twice, was seven found in the separations or were the separations fitted to seven?

pesachim/105.question: If havdala is delayed so that Shabbat will not seem like a burden, why does Rav Huna warn that even a sip of water before it brings a fatal illness?

pesachim/107.question: If beer could count as the wine of the province the second year, what made the first year's fast necessary, and does a standard bend to what a place can actually supply?

pesachim/108.question: If awe of a teacher can cancel the one night built around acting free, why does a son eating with his father, or an apprentice with his craftsman, still have to recline?

pesachim/109.question: If Passover night is declared safe from demons, why do the other Sages still look for ways to make four cups not count as an even number?

pesachim/110.question: If the danger only reaches those who take it seriously, why can an important person not simply stop taking it seriously?

pesachim/114.question: Once a voice from Heaven can be disregarded, what makes Beit Hillel's reasons about the wine and the day strong enough to settle the order?

pesachim/115.question: If matza swallowed whole counts even when it is never tasted, but matza that never touches the mouth counts as nothing, what makes an act count as eating at all?

pesachim/116.question: If the verse does not require pointing at the matza, why must it still be held up where everyone can see it?

pesachim/118.question: If the sea asks for a guarantor because a servant cannot bring a claim against his master, what is a second servant's word actually worth?

pesachim/119.question: Does David take the cup because he has nothing to name against himself, or only because he is willing to hold it while the others each found a reason to refuse?

pesachim/120.question: Why should the meal count as unbroken because one person stayed awake, when the sleepers left the table just as completely as if all had slept?

pesachim/121.question: If thanks for reaching this time belongs to whoever gains from the moment, and the study hall assigns it to the father, what does he gain by paying out five sela that the priest who receives them does not?

shekalim/3.question: If the one proof that a court may take a man's entire field is a decree aimed at people who ignored a summons, what permits using it against a farmer whose only offense was how he planted?

shekalim/4.question: If a gentile's money can end up in the Temple's service vessels once his intent was for Heaven, what is the refusal at the start of the page still refusing?

shekalim/7.question: If a sage's words are already remembrance enough that Rabban Simeon ben Gamliel would raise no stone, why must the name be spoken with them for Rebbi Joḥanan to be satisfied?

shekalim/9.question: If coins become mere leftovers the moment nobody can tell which ones were already scooped, is money set apart for the offerings defined by what happened to it or by what anyone can still know about it?

shekalim/13.question: If the rule freeing animal feed from demai was written for the owner's convenience, what is left of that convenience when the animal meant to eat refuses the food?

shekalim/18.question: If a possible mix-up of unusable money is ignored while a certain one spoils everything in the box, what makes a worry real enough to stop people from spending what is there?

shekalim/20.question: If the court can switch larceny against sacred property on and off depending on whether people are healing their wounds with the ashes, is that status a fact about the ashes or a tool for managing what people do?

yoma/3.question: If the seven days come from the inauguration but none of the inauguration's other requirements come with them, what is actually being derived besides a number?

yoma/4.question: If the Sages could add the sprinkling on their own authority, why do the seven days of removal need a source in Aaron's inauguration or in Moses' six days at all?

yoma/7.question: If Rav Naḥman keeps his rule by rereading every bull, ram and sheep on the list as an unusual case, can that list still count as evidence against him?

yoma/9.question: If the later generation kept studying Torah under foreign rule, why should the absence of a rebuilt Temple settle which generation was greater?

yoma/11.question: If who must fix a mezuza is settled by asking who needs the promised long life, does the reward, rather than the wording of the verse, decide how far a commandment reaches?

yoma/12.question: If standing in for a single day leaves a man unable to serve as High Priest or as a common priest, was being raised in holiness a gift to him or a cost?

yoma/19.question: If no one can watch the High Priest alone inside, is an oath extracted by suspicion worth the harm the elders admit they do by suspecting an innocent man?

yoma/20.question: Once need can pull the hour back to midnight, or to the first watch, what does "until morning" still require of the priests?

yoma/24.question: If almost every act in the Temple has another act waiting after it, what makes one step count as a finished thing and the step beside it only preparation?

yoma/26.question: Why should a blessing promised in a verse land on the rare service rather than the frequent one, and why is wealth treated as a limited thing that has to be shared out priest by priest?

yoma/28.question: If the hour of Abraham's afternoon prayer depends on being able to tell that the sun has begun to fall, is such a law fixed by the true moment or by what an ordinary person can see?

yoma/32.question: When each argument collapses, is the gold holier because it serves all year, or the linen because it alone enters the innermost chamber?

yoma/33.question: If clearing five lamps and then the other two exists to enliven the crowd in the courtyard, is that reason weighty enough to decide where the spare words of a verse get assigned?

yoma/35.question: Does pointing to Hillel, who kept studying while poor, prove that the poor man who says his days went to earning bread could have done the same?

yoma/40.question: When a sage answers a question about the law with a worry about how his answer will be used, may the ruling he never gave be counted as his position?

yoma/42.question: If Rabbi Yitzhak could keep the distinction between the two slaughters but lose which side was which, is a rule still usable once what it separates has been forgotten?

yoma/43.question: If no rule says when one verse's condition carries over to the next stage, is the list of who may perform each stage a settled law, or only the best reading of the words anyone has managed so far?

yoma/46.question: If a coal stops being altar fire only because it was carried down to serve a commandment, can a person's purpose change what a thing is?

yoma/48.question: Does the High Priest's hand become a vessel while it is doing a vessel's work, or does it stay only a hand?

yoma/51.question: If the Torah itself hands the other priests a share in the bull, why does the verse have to be repeated to disqualify a bull he bought with their money?

yoma/53.question: If one man walking home can turn the rain off and on, what is left of the prayer said once a year in the Holy of Holies?

yoma/54.question: If exile makes the Divine Presence hidden again rather than gone, is that concealment a punishment or a sign that the marriage still holds?

yoma/56.question: If the man performing the service is assumed too faint to tell a large bowl from a small one, why is the whole day's work still placed in his hands rather than made simpler for him?

yoma/58.question: When a verse makes a person walk past the thing he could do right now and come back to it later, has the duty to act at once been kept or only overruled?

yoma/60.question: Is an act placed by where the person stands while doing it, or by where it is headed, once the page settles the incense case on what the mishna leaves unsaid?

yoma/62.question: If the lottery is done outside the goats and never touches them, why does the page count its absence as something missing in the animal itself rather than in the order of the day's service?

yoma/64.question: When one text's wording supports Rav and another's supports Rabbi Yoḥanan, what is left to decide whether something that once fell out of use can be taken up again?

yoma/65.question: If a rabbinic precaution is not reason enough to make an animal die rather than graze, why does the last reason, itself a precaution about the goat's age, escape that objection?

yoma/66.question: If Rabbi Eliezer's refusal to speak beyond what his teacher told him is honorable, what makes the Sages' plain answers to those same questions right?

yoma/67.question: Is a sign of forgiveness worth keeping once its bad news has to be hidden from the very people it was meant to reassure?

yoma/69.question: If refusing to say what they could not see excused Jeremiah and Daniel for dropping words Moses had set, what keeps a fixed prayer binding on someone whose own experience contradicts its words?

yoma/77.question: If the coals cooling is the only reason anyone survived, does a good outcome excuse a messenger who did not do what he was told?

yoma/80.question: If Abaye concedes that the same amount settles one person greatly and another barely, is the fixed measure tracking the relief a person actually feels, or only giving the law a line it can draw?

yoma/81.question: When a teacher announces in public that drinking vinegar brings no punishment, and a crowd then drinks vinegar on the fast, is the fault in their hearing or in what he chose to say?

yoma/84.question: If Rabbi Yoḥanan told the healer at the outset that he would publish her remedy anyway, what was she agreeing to when she made him swear?

yoma/85.question: Shmuel himself says that for saving a life one acts on the doubt, so if the majority is reliable enough to decide that the child may be fed non-kosher food, why is it not reliable enough to decide whether anyone digs for him?

sukkah/2.question: If the twenty cubit limit holds whichever of the three reasons is right, and holds in a case none of them explains, is a rule kept because of its reason or apart from it?

sukkah/9.question: Does a booth built with no thought of the festival become set apart for God once the festival arrives, or is it only treated as if it had been built for that?

sukkah/10.question: If they truly owed no night in a sukka, does a ruling a person holds but keeps quiet about still bind him in the very place it applies?

sukkah/14.question: If the Sages can say those boards were only a reminder of a commandment no one could keep, what tells a person whether they are performing an obligation or only remembering it?

sukkah/15.question: If lifting the boards is enough to count as preparing the roof, why does that same lifting change nothing once the worry is that the hut still looks like a house?

sukkah/16.question: Once the argument is that a hanging partition fails where the penalty is severe, what is left of that argument when Tzippori relied on hanging sheets for exactly that prohibition, on the word of one other sage?

sukkah/17.question: If the smallest sukka is judged by how much fit roofing is left over a person's head, why is a larger one judged flaw by separate flaw instead of by that same total?

sukkah/21.question: If an ox's skin and flesh count as a shelter because they protect its own innards, why would a person's own skin not do the same for him?

sukkah/23.question: If Rabbi Meir presumes an absent husband is still alive so his wife may keep eating teruma, why would a tied animal be too likely to die to serve as a wall?

sukkah/24.question: Is a wall a wall because of what holds it up, or because a person decided to put it there?

sukkah/25.question: If the answer is that the groom's distraction comes from a mitzva and the shipwrecked man's does not, is the excuse from reciting Shema there for the man who cannot concentrate, or for the mitzva he is already busy with?

sukkah/26.question: If sleep cannot be split into short and long when it comes to the sukka, how can the same sleep be measured at a hundred cubits when phylacteries are worn?

sukkah/27.question: If a teacher will only repeat what he himself was taught, what happens to every question no teacher has yet been asked?

sukkah/30.question: If hating robbery in a burnt offering is meant to keep people far from robbery, what is left of that once despair and a sale make a stolen myrtle branch lawfully the buyer's own?

sukkah/33.question: If the same principle about whether a disqualification is permanent is accepted when it binds a person to do more and doubted when it lets a branch back in, is the argument really about the object at all?

sukkah/34.question: If the names of things can trade places within a few generations, what makes a description of red stems and smooth leaves any safer as a way of knowing what the verse asked for?

sukkah/36.question: If the same dark etrog counts as beautiful in one country and not in another, is the beauty required here a fact about the fruit or a judgment made by the people who grew up seeing other fruit?

sukkah/37.question: If tying a string to a short hyssop branch makes the string count as part of the branch, why does a cloth wrapped around a hand not count as part of the hand?

sukkah/38.question: If Josiah is credited with reading words that Shaphan read aloud to him, why can an adult male's recitation stand in for another man's while a slave's, a woman's, or a minor's must be echoed word for word?

sukkah/42.question: If a child's slaughtering is accepted only while an adult stands over him, is his readiness measured by what he can do on his own or by what he can do with someone watching?

sukkah/43.question: If the branches reached the altar only because bystanders who did not know the rules pulled them out from under stones, was the day's obligation kept or merely rescued?

sukkah/44.question: If a law given at Sinai can be forgotten in exile and then put back by prophets, whose law is it afterward?

sukkah/46.question: Once the act an object was reserved for has been carried out, is the object still set apart because the day it belonged to is not over, or does it become ordinary the instant it has served?

sukkah/48.question: If the salt did not make the altar fit for service, and everyone standing there knew that, how does hiding the damage honor the altar?

sukkah/50.question: Moses' flute could only be made of wood, since nothing else was available to him, so can a rule drawn from a case that allowed no alternative govern cases where an alternative exists?

sukkah/53.question: If one sentence covers both Hillel walking toward the place he loves and the two scribes carried to Luz, does wanting to go somewhere change anything about where a person arrives?

sukkah/54.question: When the mishna sets forty-eight as the ceiling, is it reporting what an ordinary year actually held, or deciding that the rare years do not count?

sukkah/56.question: If the same permanent penalty on Bilga can be explained either by Miriam's contempt or by a watch arriving late, is the penalty a response to what was done, or a mark kept up so that nobody forgets the story?

beitzah/6.question: Is a thing set aside by what its owner actually had in mind before the Festival began, or by the bare fact that it could be eaten?

beitzah/8.question: When a person brings in earth for one purpose, is what he may later do with it fixed by what he actually had in mind, or by what he would have agreed to had anyone asked him?

beitzah/10.question: If the words spoken the evening before leave the doves themselves unchanged, what makes a named fledgling one a person may handle and an unnamed one he may not?

beitzah/11.question: Does a man keep a restriction by following its words exactly, as when Rav Adda bar Ahava salts one bone and then says he prefers the next, until all his meat is salted?

beitzah/13.question: If piling onions finishes the work for tithes but not for Shabbat, is a task done when the food is ready to eat, or only when the worker has made something new?

beitzah/14.question: If a guest may refuse his host's porridge because the slaves in that house were thought careless, is the food judged by what was actually done to it or by who might have done it?

beitzah/17.question: If the man who pretends loses his food because others will copy him, while the man who knowingly cooked is left unresolved, is a rule like this aimed at the act or at what onlookers will learn to do?

beitzah/18.question: If a permission rests only on an act looking like something else, and it is then carried into a day where it cannot possibly look like that, what is left of the reason that granted it?

beitzah/19.question: If the Rabbis decide what a man knows by whether the rule appears in the Torah rather than by what he has actually been taught, is that a fair measure of anyone's knowledge?

beitzah/20.question: If Hillel's answer for the sake of peace is what nearly fixed the rule against his own school, whom did that peace serve?

beitzah/21.question: If dogs are included because feeding them is your obligation and gentiles left out because feeding them is not, does the permission follow who is hungry or who is already owed something by you?

beitzah/28.question: What does it mean for a teacher to act on a permission he will not state out loud, and can the student who saw through him do the same thing?

beitzah/29.question: If the buyers had already given up any claim to the foam, what was Abba Shaul handing back when he brought the three hundred jugs?

beitzah/30.question: If it is better that people stay unwitting sinners, does a rule that nobody is willing to say out loud still bind the people breaking it?

beitzah/36.question: Abaye blames the collapse on not obeying, so does a student owe his teacher the act before he is satisfied the ruling is right?

beitzah/37.question: If a share can only be told apart once the wine or the animal is actually divided, can that later division make it true that the share was his from the beginning?

beitzah/39.question: If the idol's flame is left permitted because people keep away from it on their own, does a rule get made only where people are expected to want the thing?

rosh-hashanah/2.question: If a single day on the throne can count as a whole year, why does an agreement to appoint a king count for no time at all, and what is it about actually ruling that the page never explains?

rosh-hashanah/5.question: If an item can sit in a list of legal obligations only because such items are habitually recited together, how does a reader tell which words in a list carry a rule and which are there out of habit?

rosh-hashanah/7.question: If the verse naming Nisan outright can be dismissed as meaning only first among the months of Haman's decree, why can't the other numbered months in Esther be read just as narrowly?

rosh-hashanah/8.question: Does freedom begin when the year is declared holy, or only when the shofar sounds and a man can actually walk home?

rosh-hashanah/9.question: If the Rabbis require all three acts, and in some years there are no slaves at all to release, can a fiftieth year stop being a Jubilee through nobody's fault?

rosh-hashanah/11.question: Does a single word shared by two verses prove as much about an event that has not happened as a verse saying one night was set aside for redemption from the beginning?

rosh-hashanah/12.question: If ordinary speech alone settles when "this year" is over, why add that he has already suffered enough, and which one actually releases him, his words or his pain?

rosh-hashanah/13.question: If the reading of "gathering" that supported the one-third rule was cut down, why does the rule stay in place while a new verse is hunted for it?

rosh-hashanah/18.question: If an oath is what makes a sentence impossible to cancel, why do study and acts of kindness still add years to the lives in Eli's house?

rosh-hashanah/20.question: If the month must be sanctified by witnesses who saw the new moon, can that testimony still mean anything once a court may push witnesses to report a sighting that never happened?

rosh-hashanah/22.question: The court hands him the coins as a gift rather than as wages he had earned, so does that make the man who took money to lie innocent, or only unpunished?

rosh-hashanah/24.question: If making an image becomes permitted once the purpose is to understand and teach, what stops that permission from covering almost anything?

rosh-hashanah/26.question: If a bull's blood no longer recalls the Golden Calf because it has changed, why is a cow's horn, cut and shaped into a shofar, not changed enough to stop recalling it?

rosh-hashanah/27.question: If what separates the shofar from the trumpets is the listener's attention rather than anything in the sound, is hearing something that happens to a person or something a person does?

rosh-hashanah/28.question: If a man can fulfill a commandment without meaning to, why should adding to one count against him only when he meant it, and only once its time has passed?

rosh-hashanah/30.question: Does a court's authority end when its members decide to stop, or only when they actually stand up?

rosh-hashanah/31.question: If the strip had stopped turning white anyway, was hiding it from the crowds sparing them something or taking something from them?

rosh-hashanah/35.question: If the field worker is covered because his work left him no time to prepare, does another man's recitation actually become his prayer, or does it only excuse him for not having prayed?

taanit/2.question: If the words may be said only in the season when rain would be welcome, is any real difference left between mentioning rain and asking for it?

taanit/8.question: If the prayer is heard the moment the heart is set on fasting, what does the hunger add when the decree lifts and the fast is finally kept?

taanit/11.question: If going without food makes a person pious, why does the strength a scholar loses by fasting count for more than the piety he gains?

taanit/16.question: If what God saw in Nineveh was deeds, why should the day turn on whether the ash is really ash and the graves are really Jewish?

taanit/21.question: If Abba's fee box worked because nobody could see who paid and who did not, is the kindness still the same kindness once Abaye sends two Sages to watch him do it?

taanit/23.question: If Shimon ben Shetaḥ concedes that the oath itself was indefensible and Ḥoni is safe only because God answers him, is a demand on Heaven judged by whether it was right to make or by whether it worked?

taanit/24.question: If making a fig tree bear fruit out of season costs the boy his life, what makes a sage's own distress an acceptable way to pull rain out of Heaven?

taanit/26.question: If a decree holds even after the drinking it guarded against is gone, what is left of it once the hour it forbids can be counted as ne'ila instead?

taanit/27.question: If a fast is dropped because Christians rest on Sunday and might claim the Jews honor their day, is a practice set by its own reason or by how outsiders will read it?

taanit/28.question: Are these families remembered for the wood and produce they got to Jerusalem, or for the lies they told the guards to get them there?

taanit/29.question: Why should the hour a disaster begins be the better date to remember, when Rabbi Yoḥanan can point to the day the greater part of the Sanctuary actually burned?

megillah/2.question: If Rav Ashi picks the precise transmission because the other one leaves a contradiction, is a teaching's author established by evidence about who said it, or by which name makes the rulings agree?

megillah/3.question: If the dignity owed one dead stranger outranks the public reading of the miracle, why does the study of one living person rank below the Temple service?

megillah/5.question: If putting a tree in the ground is joy when it is for shade and forbidden work when it is for income, is a deed measured by what the hands do or by what the planter wants from it?

megillah/7.question: If the one proof Rava cannot refute is itself a claim about what heaven did, what could ever count as evidence that a book was divinely inspired?

megillah/8.question: Abaye settles what a word means by arguing that the verse would have said nothing if it meant the opposite, so how confident can a reader be about what a verse needed to say?

megillah/16.question: If the page itself holds that Torah study outranks saving lives, and treats Mordecai's public work as a demotion, why does the same page insist that the fasts and the crying out belong in one sentence with Esther's decree?

megillah/17.question: If fourteen years of study excuse Jacob's absence from his parents, why are the two years he lingered on the way home counted against him?

megillah/18.question: If hearing words you cannot parse still counts as publicizing the miracle, what is the listener actually receiving?

megillah/20.question: If a boy's memory of reading is refused, and so is the approval of the sage who already permits it, what evidence could ever show that minors reading the Megilla was accepted?

megillah/22.question: Is the worry that a latecomer will misjudge what he missed reason enough to cut in half a verse that was handed down whole?

megillah/24.question: If seeing the Chariot in the mind is enough to expound it, why does Rabbi Yehuda hold that a blessing depends on benefit actually received and not on understanding?

megillah/25.question: If Aaron's explanation is held back because, as the page says, it did more damage than the act itself, why is it still read aloud in Hebrew, as though words stop being dangerous once the crowd cannot follow them?

megillah/27.question: If the new scroll is no less holy than the old, what is left for the rule about rising holiness to protect?

moed-katan/3.question: If Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel attached to their own decree permission for anyone later to cancel it, in what sense were people bound by it while it stood?

moed-katan/6.question: If the penalty had to grow from free weeding to losing the entire harvest, was the owner being punished for sowing mixed seeds or for enjoying the court's help?

moed-katan/9.question: If rejoicing is incomplete without eating and drinking, is the people's feasting part of the dedication itself, or a human appetite that the dedication was permitted to satisfy?

moed-katan/11.question: Once the page grants that an important person should be stricter than the law requires, what keeps that extra strictness from being paid for by a partner who never chose it?

moed-katan/14.question: If the belt settles the matter because any passerby can see it, why does the craftsman whose customers watched him searching all day remain a doubtful case, and does a rule about appearances count what people already know or only what they can see at the moment?

moed-katan/15.question: If a court can put a person under ostracism whenever it decides to, why can no one here say what that person may and may not do, while verses settle the leper's case?

moed-katan/16.question: If the scholar never said the word ostracism and the woman learned she owed a day only by asking Rav Nahman, is a ban something laid on a person or something the person takes on herself?

moed-katan/21.question: If the public's need is what permits a mourner to teach, why must his words still pass through two other mouths, as though the permission comes only on condition that he stay visibly diminished?

moed-katan/24.question: If the mourning that stops on Shabbat is the mourning other people can see, why must the bed be set upright inside the house while going barefoot, which anyone on the street would notice, stays the mourner's own choice?

moed-katan/25.question: If Rav Huna's own conduct on his bed can cancel an honor the Sages wanted to give him, why should the rules he taught them be imposed on a body that can no longer object?

moed-katan/27.question: If the way to spare the poor and the sick their shame is to make everyone's burial look exactly like theirs, does that give them honor, or only keep them from being noticed?

chagigah/2.question: If a man is freed for the world's good rather than for his own sake, why is he the one left paying for it?

chagigah/3.question: Once the exemption rests on being unable to teach others rather than unable to learn, why should coming to hear the Torah read depend on what a person can pass on instead of what he can take in?

chagigah/4.question: Is releasing the tanner and the dung gatherer from the pilgrimage a kindness to them, or an arrangement made for everyone who would rather not stand near them?

chagigah/9.question: Is a person called crooked because of harm that no later act can undo, or because he once stood straight and then fell?

chagigah/15.question: If Rabbi Yoḥanan believed a sage who strays can be held by the hand and pulled back, was Aḥer's refusal to repent his own choice or the Divine Voice's doing?

chagigah/17.question: If seven days was chosen because it is the cautious guess rather than the proven one, is that a ruling or an admission that nobody knows?

chagigah/18.question: If the Torah forbids work on the middle days but says only that work preventing loss is allowed, what exactly was forbidden before the Sages decided which labors those were?

chagigah/20.question: If Rabbi Yishmael's questioning found an actual contact in both weaving cases, does an unguarded mind by itself make a cloth impure, or does it only mean something probably touched it unnoticed?

chagigah/22.question: Does an unexplained ruling deserve the trust Rabbi Yehoshua gave Beit Shammai only after a student supplied its reason, or was his doubt what drew that reason out?

chagigah/23.question: When nothing has actually touched the food, can breaking the Sages' decree by itself make it impure, as Rabbi Ila says, or does impurity come only from contact, as Rabbi Zeira says?

chagigah/25.question: If the Sages could suspend their own decree about the plowed-over grave for the sake of the paschal offering, why does their decree on Samaritan land stand even when the oil is meant for the Temple?

chagigah/26.question: If the wine counted as pure only as long as the Festival lasted, was it ever pure, or only treated as pure?

yevamot/3.question: If a rival wife is forbidden only where a brother could actually have married the widow, does the reach of a prohibition depend on how grave it is or on the obligation it blocks?

yevamot/4.question: Does a verse sitting out of place, or carrying a word to spare, actually prove anything, or does it only give permission to read what someone already wanted to read?

yevamot/5.question: If one unusual word can establish that a positive command overrides a prohibition, why can three commands that actually set aside a penalty as severe as karet establish nothing?

yevamot/6.question: If the errand of driving the animal counts only as preparation and not as honoring a father, at what point does fetching what he needs become the honoring itself?

yevamot/8.question: If the forbidden sister stays forbidden everywhere while her rival wife is forbidden only where the brother is obliged to marry, why should a duty to marry one woman be the thing that makes another woman forbidden?

yevamot/12.question: If the mishna's exact wording was precise enough to prove the law, what is left of that proof once the wording is changed to fit a different ruling?

yevamot/13.question: How does a house that calls the other house's marriages licentious keep marrying that house's daughters?

yevamot/18.question: If a brother may wait until marrying the widow has become impossible, why should the tie still bind him after the widow herself has died?

yevamot/20.question: If the first act of intercourse is the very obligation that overrides the prohibition, can the Sages forbid a man from doing his duty because of what he might do the day after he has done it?

yevamot/23.question: If the danger named in the verse is that a gentile parent turns the child away from God, why should it matter which parent is the gentile one?

yevamot/25.question: If being a robber under Torah law makes a man unfit to report that a husband died, why does announcing "I killed him" leave him fit, as though a man's own words about himself count for less than what others can prove about him?

yevamot/28.question: If a case counts simply because someone can construct one, is a rule still about what happens, or only about what can be described?

yevamot/29.question: If a man's power to cancel her vows rests on the food he owes her rather than on any marriage between them, what makes someone a husband?

yevamot/30.question: Since Rav Nahman and Rav Ashi split over whether that untouched tie already counts, is an obligation nobody has yet acted on already a bond between two people, or only a claim waiting to become one?

yevamot/31.question: If a written date stays in place only when the person holding the document gains from it, is the requirement protecting anyone, or only recording what one side already wants?

yevamot/32.question: If one and the same permission can be described either as given to priests or as given to the Temple, what decides which description is right, and should a man's guilt double or stay single because of that choice?

yevamot/39.question: If the preference flipped back to marriage because the Rabbis' reading was adopted and not because brothers' intentions improved, can a rule set in response to how people actually behaved be reversed while their behavior stays the same?

yevamot/40.question: If a reciter's own correction stays inside the baraita he passes on, how can anyone later tell what he was taught from what he fixed?

yevamot/44.question: If the elders are supposed to steer a man away from a marriage likely to bring discord, why is being one of four wives, visited once a month, not discord enough?

yevamot/51.question: If Abaye's reading lets a second act count only when it differs in kind from the first, is a legal act measured by what it changes for the woman or by what sort of act it is?

yevamot/53.question: If a man asleep acquires a wife through an act he never chose, what makes intercourse an acquiring act at all rather than something he has to intend?

yevamot/54.question: If coercion by others does not stop this marriage from taking effect, why does it still matter that the man meant to perform some act of intercourse, when his aim need not be at her, at marriage, or even at a person?

yevamot/55.question: When two people report the same teacher and say opposite things, why does Rav Dimi reach for lying rather than for a faulty memory?

yevamot/56.question: When Shmuel keeps his rule by rewriting the teaching that contradicts it, has the objection been answered or only rewritten away?

yevamot/60.question: When one sage says a ruling is the law and another orders the man who relied on it to divorce, whose word is the law for that man?

yevamot/61.question: If the Gemara thinks the appointment was purchased, why does the mishna still rely on this marriage to prove the law?

yevamot/62.question: If the earth being inhabited is the whole standard, why should it matter that two grandchildren come from one child rather than from two?

yevamot/65.question: If the command to have children binds only the man, whose interest is it actually measuring, when a childless woman's plea that she will need care in old age is enough to force her husband to divorce her and pay?

yevamot/66.question: When an early teaching supports one side and a stated reason supports the other, what makes the reason the stronger ground for a ruling?

yevamot/67.question: If the Rabbis admitted that the ruling Rabbi Yosei received from Shemaya and Avtalyon was sound and still did not follow it, what is a ruling handed down from teachers worth to those who hear it?

yevamot/68.question: If intercourse with a man of unfit lineage disqualifies a priest's daughter because she is holy in herself, does it change an Israelite woman who was never holy and eats teruma only through her son, or does it only change whose food she may eat?

yevamot/70.question: When two different disqualifications both fit the shared phrase and the sages pick between them by judging which failing is graver, is the rule coming from the verse or from their own sense of what is serious?

yevamot/71.question: If a rule can only be tested by imagining a baby kept alive seven days by his mother's fever, is the law being measured against lives people actually live, or against whatever cannot be ruled out?

yevamot/74.question: If one ranking is settled by saying that death at the hand of Heaven outweighs everything else, and the next by counting which list of severities is longer, what makes a food stricter, the weight of its worst penalty or the number of its rules?

yevamot/75.question: If a man crushed from birth may marry because no human hand caused it, yet Mar bar Rav Ashi's cutting makes an injured man fit, is the bar about how the body came to be damaged or about what it can do now?

yevamot/76.question: If Abner's reason for permitting a Moabite woman fails under Doeg's objection, what can the study hall rely on when it repeats the ruling?

yevamot/80.question: The page says a whole-body defect is unlike one bad eye, but why should the extent of a defect decide whether a stretch of time nobody watched can be presumed unchanged?

yevamot/81.question: If a cake of teruma figs can disappear into a hundred ordinary ones, is that because the rule protecting it is weak, or because a single cake was never important enough to count?

yevamot/82.question: Why keep a teaching on the record under Rav Ashi's name once the argument has called it plainly mistaken?

yevamot/83.question: If seven children are not proof that the man from Biri could father children, can a rule about what a whole class of people cannot do ever be disproved by one person doing it?

yevamot/84.question: If the law forbids a priest to marry a woman disqualified from the priesthood, why is the reverse match hers to choose, and is a standing a person is born with hers to give up?

yevamot/86.question: If Elazar ben Azarya could still eat the tithe whenever an owner chose to hand it over, why was it worth a wall and a new gate to deny him the right to take it himself?

yevamot/87.question: The page answers that the verses about the priest's daughter spell out limits while the verses about the other woman do not, so is a rule more generous toward whoever it says less about?

yevamot/88.question: If one witness is believed because otherwise she could be left unable ever to remarry, why does the cost of a mistake fall on her rather than on the witness whose word was wrong?

yevamot/92.question: If the court was only mistaken about the facts, why is a single witness believed here when one witness is never enough anywhere else in the Torah?

yevamot/95.question: If Shmuel's ruling is the only thing keeping the man's wife permitted to him, what is Rav Yehuda doing by telling him the sentence he was not allowed to impose?

yevamot/96.question: Does a teaching keep its teacher present because his name is spoken with it, or because the teaching is his whether anyone says so or not?

yevamot/99.question: If a careful witness's words have to be reread so that no error occurred, is the promise about the righteous a claim about what happened or a rule about how their stories may be told?

yevamot/100.question: If doubt about who his father is blocks him from claiming either man's property, why does the same doubt not block the two men from dividing his?

yevamot/101.question: If three judges were already enough and the other two stand there only so people notice, why should being a convert keep a man out of a place the law never required be filled?

yevamot/103.question: If the same wooden support counts as a shoe on one man and as a foot on another, is a thing defined by what it is made of, by what it protects, or by whose body it sits on?

yevamot/104.question: Is a loaf that can be neither redeemed nor eaten a fair picture of a widow who may not marry a brother and is not yet free to marry anyone else?

yevamot/109.question: If a minor's refusal is discouraged because she may grow up and regret rejecting a husband who suited her, does arranging that refusal so the widow can be married make the regret any less hers?

yevamot/114.question: If a child who acts because he knows what his father wants counts as the father's own doing, why is the man who walks children past his lost keys any different?

yevamot/115.question: If a matching amount of sesame identifies nothing because two barrels could hold the same by chance, what makes a name enough to prove that the dead man is this Yitzḥak and no other?

yevamot/119.question: Should a woman wait indefinitely rather than perform ḥalitza, the shoe-removal rite that releases her, just so nobody who watched the ceremony and missed the later announcement draws the wrong conclusion?

yevamot/120.question: If wax on a forehead was enough to hide Abba bar Marta from the men he owed money, how certain can a witness ever be that the face he saw was the face he thinks it was?

yevamot/122.question: If the danger is that a woman remarries while her husband still lives, how can the money of her marriage contract be what decides that her witness need not be cross-examined?

ketubot/3.question: If undoing a marriage made with money takes only declaring the coins ownerless, what sort of power is it that undoes the other kind by renaming an act already finished?

ketubot/4.question: If keeping the couple apart exists only to stop a mourner who was granted his feast from growing careless about everything else, is that separation itself a mourning practice or just a fence around one?

ketubot/6.question: Given the page's answer that only an unfinished obligation excuses a wandering mind, why should a grief already suffered scatter a person any less?

ketubot/8.question: Does telling Rav Ḥiyya bar Abba that he was righteous enough to lose a child for his generation's sins comfort him, or only inform him that the blow was aimed past him?

ketubot/10.question: If a groom is believed because no one would waste the cost of his own wedding feast, why do the rabbis keep searching for another explanation instead of taking him at his word?

ketubot/19.question: If documents of trust were common enough that Rav Kahana had to forbid keeping one in the house, why is it assumed that no witness would have signed one?

ketubot/24.question: If the only grounds for believing these men are the punishment they risk and the fact that others are watching, does that establish who a man is, or only what he is unwilling to dare?

ketubot/25.question: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi trusts the father only where the father could act on his own anyway, so is a claim about who a person is the kind of thing that can be half believed?

ketubot/29.question: If the fine goes to the father, why should the young woman's death before the trial cancel a payment that was never hers?

ketubot/31.question: If one reason says the landing could not happen without the shot and the other says the arrow cannot be called back, is a stretch of motion a single deed because its parts depend on each other, or because the person can no longer stop it?

ketubot/33.question: Once severity is settled by whether the lashes have a fixed limit, is a punishment's harshness a property of the sentence itself, or of how much the person facing it would surrender to avoid it?

ketubot/34.question: The page explains that where the theft itself carries no payment the added fine for slaughter falls away with it, but does a debt incurred a moment earlier become any more real than one born in the same act?

ketubot/36.question: If the same redeemed captive is presumed a virgin when a fine is owed but not when priestly food is eaten, does the presumption describe her or what someone gains by it?

ketubot/37.question: Is the claim that a captive protected herself a statement about what she actually did, or a decision to assume the best because the alternative would keep her from marrying?

ketubot/38.question: If her father still collects the money of a later betrothal after she was divorced, what is left of the claim that the divorce ended his authority over her?

ketubot/47.question: If the Sages believed a husband would not ransom his wife unless he were paid in produce first, is the duty they built on that suspicion still a duty?

ketubot/52.question: If a husband made his own promise impossible to keep, does the obligation he took on when he made it still bind him?

ketubot/56.question: If the wife keeps only a hundred dinars whether she signs or merely says so, what is the written receipt protecting when the money it reports never changed hands?

ketubot/59.question: If a konam is strong enough to cancel a creditor's hold on mortgaged property, why should the husband's claim on her earnings hold out against it only because the Sages chose to strengthen it?

ketubot/60.question: If four authorities permit betrothal at fifteen months, what makes the stricter count of Rav and Shmuel the one Abaye chased his tenant farmer through the sand to impose?

ketubot/61.question: If pouring his cup and washing his feet count as affection rather than work, can affection be owed the way chores are owed?

ketubot/64.question: If the smallest allowance a wife is owed must include food for a visitor who may never come, is the amount fixed by what she needs or by what a household is expected to be able to offer a stranger?

ketubot/67.question: If the verse obliges a community to supply whatever a poor person is accustomed to, down to a servant running ahead of him, is a man's habit of fatty meat and aged wine a claim on others or a fault in him?

ketubot/74.question: If a dissolved vow means she was never bound at all, is a condition a claim about the facts at the moment it was set, or about what the man will actually have to live with?

ketubot/76.question: When nobody can establish whether the blemishes came before the betrothal or the donkey died before the trade, is it fairer to leave the money with whoever is already holding it, or to charge the one in whose keeping the trouble first appeared?

ketubot/77.question: Whose claim is the court serving when it ends a marriage both people want, for the sake of children who do not exist?

ketubot/79.question: If the old trees and aging slaves will be used up and leave her holding nothing, is she better served by the money they would fetch or by keeping what came from her paternal family?

ketubot/80.question: If the husband holds the produce of his wife's land only because the house gains by it, does selling those rights become permitted the moment the money he receives feeds the house?

ketubot/83.question: If the husband chose the broad words and the wife holding the document is the one who loses by their vagueness, what stops a man from writing generously and meaning almost nothing?

ketubot/84.question: If Rabbi Akiva is right that mercy has no place in judgment, is a rule the Sages wrote to favor wives anything other than mercy turned into law?

ketubot/86.question: If a debt is owed to the original creditor alone, and he can cancel it whenever he likes, what did the men who paid for the document actually buy?

ketubot/87.question: If the oath exists because whoever receives money remembers it loosely, does a woman who can account for every last small coin prove her honesty, or only show that she has prepared her story?

ketubot/91.question: If each son's share is fixed by what the estate was worth on the day the father died, why did Rav Amram press the sons with the larger claim to give some of it up, and threaten them when they refused?

ketubot/94.question: When ownership cannot be settled by the deeds, is splitting the field between the two claimants fairer than trusting a judge's sense of what the mother wanted, given that the same sense produced opposite rulings?

ketubot/97.question: If undoing a sale made under pressure is safe only because such emergencies are rare, what justifies the rule in a place where the emergency is admitted to be common?

ketubot/98.question: When someone does part of what they were authorized to do and part they were not, does the authorized part remain valid, or does the overreach cancel all of it?

ketubot/99.question: Is the room judges get for a mistaken appraisal a privilege of their office, and if so why should the widow or an agent selling the same land get none?

ketubot/102.question: If the spoken promises already bind the fathers completely, what does putting them in a document add that Rav Ashi is unwilling to grant?

ketubot/106.question: If trading the money set aside for the poor could make it grow, is having it ready the moment someone asks worth more than having more of it?

ketubot/111.question: If Jacob, certain of his own righteousness, still doubted he would merit the tunnels, can anyone treat a promise like that as something to rely on?

ketubot/112.question: If Rabbi Hanina filled potholes so no traveler would speak ill of the land, was Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi honoring it or harming it when he asked it to produce less?

nedarim/2.question: The mishna says that "I am ostracized from you" does not clearly declare anything forbidden, so why does Rabbi Akiva's own uncertainty push him toward binding the speaker rather than leaving him free?

nedarim/4.question: If a nazirite's closing offering neither wipes away a wrongdoing nor permits anything, the way a new mother's offering lets her eat consecrated food, why should finishing a vow well cost an animal at all?

nedarim/5.question: If clear wording is demanded in a bill of divorce because the marriage must be fully severed, why should half-said words be enough to cut a man off from his neighbor?

nedarim/6.question: If the second woman cannot tell from "and you" whether she is now betrothed, should her status depend on what the man meant or on what his words can be understood to say?

nedarim/8.question: If every dream carries idle matter, why does that doubt cancel the dream's release and never the dream's excommunication, leaving the man bound by the half that harms him?

nedarim/11.question: When someone ties his food to a thing that was once forbidden and now is not, is he bound by what the thing is or by what it was?

nedarim/12.question: If every proof can be turned aside by rereading its wording, what could settle whether a person's words reach back to a status the meat no longer has?

nedarim/13.question: If a firstborn animal is holy from birth whether or not its owner ever says so, does the command that he declare it holy add anything real?

nedarim/16.question: If context can twist any wording into its opposite, and the fixed principle wins for that very reason, what happens to a man held to words that everyone in the room knew he meant the other way?

nedarim/18.question: If the same words bind a man in Judea and leave him free in the Galilee, is he held to what he meant or to what his neighbors would have meant?

nedarim/22.question: If the anger Rav Seḥora provoked counts as a fact he never considered when he vowed, could almost anything that happens afterward undo a promise?

nedarim/25.question: If listing all six hundred thirteen commandments would have left no room to twist the words, is sparing the people that trouble a good enough reason to accept an oath they could read narrowly?

nedarim/26.question: Why should a vow stand or fall on words the man never actually said, only words he claims he would have said had he known his father was there?

nedarim/27.question: If the man at the river genuinely could not cross, why should it matter that a ferry's position could have been anticipated, when an illness no one planned for frees the man who promised to come eat?

nedarim/29.question: If a man's words to God bind him the moment he speaks, with nothing handed over and no one standing there to receive it, in what sense is the ox not yet consecrated during those thirty days?

nedarim/30.question: If common usage decides what a vow forbids, what happens to the person who chose his words precisely and meant something narrower than those words usually mean?

nedarim/34.question: If a man's words keep a loaf forbidden to his neighbor even after he no longer owns it, why should who owned what at the moment of the vow decide anything at all?

nedarim/35.question: Is a priest at the altar doing something for the person whose birds he offers, or only serving Heaven, a question the page raises and then leaves open?

nedarim/36.question: If the father's promise gave the winning child no portion of the lamb at all, was he keeping his word or only using it?

nedarim/37.question: If the same hour with a child can be paid for as minding him but not as teaching him, what makes watching a service worth money while teaching is not?

nedarim/38.question: If what Moses gave away was analysis he could teach without having any less of it, why is he described as a man handing out his own bread?

nedarim/42.question: Once the page settles that "my property" covers only what the man still owns, why should the word he happened to choose, rather than what he meant to forbid, decide whether the ban stays on fruit he no longer owns?

nedarim/47.question: If a wife with no other way to eat may borrow and have her creditors collect from her husband, and fruit forbidden in a tree's first three years can be sold to fund a valid betrothal, what is left of a ban that holds only before the fact and not after?

nedarim/48.question: If a handover of property counts only when it takes effect at once, can anything be given on a condition that may never arrive?

nedarim/49.question: If a vow means whatever the vower's neighbors mean by the word, what binds a man who made his vow in one town and sat down to eat in another?

nedarim/51.question: When a vow is read by what its words ordinarily mean rather than by what the man had in mind, is he bound by his own promise or by other people's habits of speech?

nedarim/54.question: If what a vow forbids is decided by what an agent sent shopping would stop and ask about, is the man bound by the words he said or by other people's habits of speech?

nedarim/55.question: If Rava sent Rav Yosef a question he believed he could already answer, was he honoring his teacher or using him, and which of the two did Rav Yosef hear?

nedarim/57.question: If growth outweighing the original settles the matter when the result is more obligation but proves nothing when the result would be permission, is that a claim about what happens to the onion, or only a rule for how to act while nobody knows?

nedarim/58.question: Once a forbidden onion has been replanted and grown again, is it still the same onion that was forbidden, or has the new growth made it a different thing?

nedarim/60.question: If Rabbi Natan counts the keeping of the vow as worse than the making of it, what is a man's own word worth once he has spoken it?

nedarim/62.question: If a person may say who he is when his life is in danger, why is paying the farmer off with money a cleaner rescue than being known for learning?

nedarim/64.question: If the men seeking Moses' life only lost their property and their standing, why is that loss enough to call them dead and not enough to count as a new circumstance releasing him from his vow?

nedarim/65.question: If the Sanhedrin's only error was dissolving the oath outside Nebuchadnezzar's presence, what good would dissolving it in his presence have done Zedekiah?

nedarim/66.question: Is Rabbi Yehuda right that one couple's peace is worth a scholar's dignity, or Rabbi Shimon right that tasting the food only teaches the next husband to vow the same way?

nedarim/68.question: Is a vow one force that can be made weaker, or a set of separate prohibitions that can be removed one at a time, and why should that difference decide whether she is flogged?

nedarim/73.question: If a woman's vows are made with the consent of the man who feeds her already in mind, is such a vow ever fully her own?

nedarim/75.question: If a ritual bath can remove impurity but cannot prevent it, is canceling a vow already spoken the same kind of power as keeping a vow from ever taking hold?

nedarim/78.question: If the only difference between the two silent husbands is what each privately intends, why should an intention he never states stretch his power past the single day?

nedarim/79.question: If a day of silence is enough to make a wife's vow permanent, while cancelling it requires the husband to say so before nightfall, is a decision reached by doing nothing the same kind of decision as one made on purpose?

nedarim/81.question: If the same grime is deadly when measured by what it does to a body and negligible when measured by what a husband minds, which measure decides whether a woman is being harmed?

nedarim/83.question: If the pain of never burying others is only her distress about how she herself will be treated after death, why does that count as deprivation the same way being kept from wine does now?

nedarim/84.question: If what turns the grain into a benefit is the owner's power to choose who receives it, is a gift defined by what changes hands or by the giver's freedom to hand it elsewhere?

nedarim/85.question: If the page never produces a source for a vow that waits until divorce to take hold, what makes a person's word today bind a life she is not yet living?

nedarim/89.question: Was the failing student's vow actually void, or did Rav Aḥa bar Rav Huna decide the man should marry and let him believe what was convenient?

nedarim/90.question: If the same claim is refused for the divorce and accepted for the food only because ordinary food remains open to her, has anyone actually decided whether she is telling the truth?

nazir/2.question: If giving up wine is itself counted as a transgression, in what sense can the man holding his hair be calling himself beautiful?

nazir/3.question: When one phrase counts as a vow only because the man was holding his hair, and another counts on the strength of a verse alone, is he bound by what he said or by what he was seen doing?

nazir/5.question: If bar Padda counts only twenty-nine days yet the restrictions hold on the thirtieth until the offerings are brought, is the man still a nazirite on a day his term does not include?

nazir/9.question: If the words a man adds show he never wanted the vow he began, is he held to what he first said or freed by what he meant?

nazir/11.question: If the same sentence binds one speaker to everything and binds a drunk speaker to one cup, what does a vow actually bind, the words said or the wish behind them?

nazir/14.question: If a man interrupts his own vow to keep one he made for his son and then goes back to it, is he keeping one commitment or two, and what decides which?

nazir/18.question: Does a new term begin because a certain day has arrived, or only once the nazirite has actually done the thing that ends his impurity?

nazir/19.question: If the going without wine is itself the wrong, what is left for the husband's cancellation to undo, given that she already lived those days without it?

nazir/22.question: If two ways of copying another person's vow, And I and I am hereby like you, leave one woman bound and the other free, what is a person actually taking on when she attaches herself to someone else's promise?

nazir/23.question: If good intention can make a forbidden act worth blessing, why can the woman's bad intention not be dismissed as harmless once her husband had already freed her to drink?

nazir/26.question: If three piles of beams can stand for three separate offerings but three silver bars cannot, what makes an object hold the purpose its owner gave it?

nazir/27.question: If a son may buy his atoning animal with the coins his dead father set aside, but may never bring the animal his father already picked out, what does picking an animal do to it that setting aside coins does not do to them?

nazir/29.question: If both the training of the boy and the prohibitions it sets aside rest only on the Sages' authority, what decides which one gives way?
