nazir/30.question: Once the rule is declared unrelated to inheritance, why do the later questions about two sons and a firstborn's double portion still reason as though it were an inheritance after all?

nazir/37.question: When Rabbi Akiva and the Rabbis look at the same pot and disagree over whether it is too strange to learn a general rule from, is a case's strangeness a fact about the case or a choice the reader makes?

nazir/38.question: If disputed cases are kept off the list because they are unsettled, and the rainwater case is kept off because it was cancelled, is the count of ten a list of what everyone agrees on or a list of what still holds?

nazir/40.question: If a forbidden shaving counts however it is done, why should a commanded shaving count only when a razor does it?

nazir/42.question: Does Ravina's reason, that the first attempt failed to remove everything, also decide Abaye's case, or can cutting the missed hairs later complete an act that once failed?

nazir/43.question: If Rav Ḥisda forbids a priest to bury his father's headless body and then requires him to bury it anyway once no one else will, what is the demand for a whole body meant to preserve?

nazir/44.question: If every argument from severity is turned aside by a verse rather than defeated by reasoning, what does the mishna's ranking of severity actually decide?

nazir/47.question: If the deputy counts for less than the war priest when a life must be saved and for more when purity must be saved, is a person's importance one thing or many things at once?

nazir/48.question: If burying an unclaimed corpse pushes aside even duties whose neglect carries being cut off, what does a dead stranger have a claim to that the man's own sister does not?

nazir/49.question: If the mishna itself opens the list with a whole corpse before the olive-bulk, was Rabbi Yehuda objecting to the words or to the man who said them?

nazir/50.question: If the only thing known is that liquefied human flesh defiles, on what basis could anyone decide whether the same holds for an animal carcass?

nazir/51.question: When the only corpse that could produce qualifying dust is one prepared that strangely, is the rule still describing something that happens, or has it become a way of marking where impurity stops?

nazir/53.question: If that ruling came down intact from Haggai, Zechariah and Malachi, what were the earlier Elders arguing about?

nazir/54.question: If the Sages themselves made the decree, why is it still unsettled whether the air of land outside Eretz Yisrael makes a person impure, or only touching its ground?

sotah/3.question: If the same jealousy can be a spirit of purity or a spirit of impurity, what tells a husband which one has entered him before he warns her?

sotah/5.question: If the same husk-top image marks both the arrogant man's withering and the scholar's crown, what makes a trace of pride ruinous in one person and fitting in another?

sotah/9.question: If Gaza counts as Samson's first wrongdoing only because the earlier woman in Timnah became his wife, does a wrong shrink when it is done lawfully?

sotah/10.question: If Absalom's fear of Gehenna is what kept him hanging until he died, and he ended up there anyway until his father's crying pulled him out, can dread of punishment ever save a person from it?

sotah/11.question: If that oath against a flood was kept and Pharaoh's advisors still died by water, can anyone rely on a promise read for exactly what it says and no more?

sotah/13.question: If Judah alone moved to save Joseph and is demoted for stopping, while the brothers who never moved are not punished at all, is abandoning a good act worse than never starting one?

sotah/14.question: Can a procedure built to wear a woman down until she confesses be called protection, when the very flour placed in her hands is chosen to mark her as an animal?

sotah/15.question: If dust brought in from elsewhere counts as dust of the Sanctuary floor once it has rested there a moment, does a thing's holiness come from where it originated or from where it was last set down?

sotah/16.question: If decomposed vegetable matter is allowed because it will become dust, is a thing judged by what it is at the moment or by what it will turn into?

sotah/19.question: If the same refusal means guilt from a woman in good health and means nothing from a frightened one, is her refusal evidence about what she did, or about how she appears?

sotah/20.question: If a scribe's whole care is letters no fly can rub away, what does it mean that one passage must be written so it can be destroyed?

sotah/21.question: If merit for Torah study can pass to someone who only made that study possible, why could Shevna not buy a share of his brother's?

sotah/22.question: If keeping commandments only for the reward counts as a start toward keeping them for their own sake, why does the man who drags his feet to look humble not count as a start too?

sotah/25.question: If the husband's own warning is what gave his wife the status of a sota, what changes at the moment she secludes herself that puts the matter beyond his power to undo?

sotah/29.question: When Rabbi Yoḥanan says he does not know the reasoning behind Rabbi Yosei's inference instead of simply calling it wrong, does an argument still bind those who cannot see why its author found it convincing?

sotah/34.question: If Caleb had to beg at the graves while Joshua was protected by a prayer said for him before he ever set out, is a rescue worth more when the one rescued had to ask for it?

sotah/35.question: If the death was David's punishment and Uzzah still entered the World-to-Come, can one person's dying be another person's penalty?

sotah/37.question: If Benjamin was stoned for going out of turn and still ended up hosting the Temple, does breaking rank count as a fault at all when someone has to move first?

sotah/42.question: If the deputy, always ready to serve, is not counted as appointed because he has nothing of his own to do, is a position real only when it has work in front of it now?

sotah/43.question: If a man who has paid the owners in full still counts as holding a stolen house, can repayment ever undo what the theft made of the thing?

sotah/44.question: If the exemptions double as cover for the sinner, can any man walk home for his new house without the others wondering which reason is really his?

sotah/46.question: Is a small kindness rewarded for itself, even when the man who did it handed a whole city over to be killed?

gittin/3.question: If the page's answer is that the agent checks everything carefully because he must hand the document over in front of two or three people, does trusting one careful person protect the woman as well as denying the husband any chance to contest?

gittin/5.question: If the declaration was imposed to make things easier for the woman, can leaving it out fairly undo the marriage she then made and mark her child as illegitimate?

gittin/8.question: If one document can be believed about a man's freedom and doubted about the property it grants in the same breath, what makes a person's status easier to trust than a field?

gittin/11.question: If the slave ate the priest's teruma only because he counted as his master's property, is the food he can no longer eat once freed a real loss to him?

gittin/12.question: When a master owns a person's labor, should the cost of feeding that person fall on the master or on strangers' charity?

gittin/13.question: Can a borrower be bound to a person who was not yet born when he took the loan, or does an obligation need someone already in the world to be owed to?

gittin/15.question: If a drop and a fence of five handbreadths each are allowed to add up to ten, why can two kinds of proof not add up to one valid divorce?

gittin/16.question: If Rabbi Yehuda trusts people overseas to remember that a bill of divorce must be written for the woman's sake, why does he still fear that a split declaration will teach people to confirm ordinary documents with one witness?

gittin/17.question: If a precise date was never going to pin down the hour anyway, was the requirement ever about knowing when the divorce happened, or only about marking a rough boundary with a before and an after?

gittin/18.question: If the three months exist to keep a child's paternity clear, why should the date written on the document decide the count rather than the day the couple actually stopped living together?

gittin/19.question: Rabbi Yoḥanan refuses to carry the Shabbat ruling over into the signing of documents and gives no reason for the split, so can the same stroke of ink count as writing for one law and not for another?

gittin/20.question: If a document can be entirely hers while she is obliged to hand the paper straight back, what is it she has to own for the divorce to take effect?

gittin/23.question: If sight is needed only back when the document was written, why must the agent's mind be sound both then and at the moment he hands it over?

gittin/24.question: If a document that divorces nobody can still leave a woman unable to marry a priest, what has actually happened to her when it reaches her hand?

gittin/25.question: If the husband's own later choice cannot settle who the document was written for, why should a stranger's act be able to?

gittin/26.question: Can one rule be called a protection for abandoned wives when it delays one woman's divorce and hurries another's, depending only on which sage's view of the document is assumed?

gittin/27.question: If a mark on the document can be checked by anyone and a person's claim to recognize it cannot, why should a scholar's bare word be enough to put a divorce into a woman's hand?

gittin/32.question: If an ambiguous phrase is read in whichever sense would actually work, is that discovering what the man meant or deciding it for him?

gittin/34.question: If Giddul's blessing left no doubt that he wanted the divorce stopped, why should only the spoken words of cancellation have the power to stop it?

gittin/36.question: Shmuel would abolish the prosbol if he were strong enough, yet he still rules on which courts may write one; can a judge keep enforcing a rule he believes lets lenders take what they are not owed?

gittin/37.question: If a cancellation holds only until the borrower is coached in the words that undo it, was Abba bar Marta's debt ever really released?

gittin/38.question: If freedom is granted to the one woman because no husband was possible for her and withheld from the other because a husband can be assigned to watch her, is freedom here something owed to the woman or only a way of stopping other people from sinning?

gittin/44.question: If the Sages set a smaller penalty for selling a slave because people rarely do it, is a penalty measured by the wrong done or by how often people are tempted to do it?

gittin/46.question: If one rule can be explained either as shielding the woman from her husband's later lie or as punishing her so that other women take vows more carefully, does it matter which reason is the right one?

gittin/48.question: Does buying a fixed run of harvests make a field yours enough to call it the land God gave you?

gittin/53.question: If the Sages excuse the accidental offender only to make sure the owner gets told, what is left of Ḥizkiyya's claim that the invisible loss was real damage to begin with?

gittin/55.question: When the Sages make it easier for a wrongdoer to turn back, how much of what he took may he keep before the easing becomes a reward?

gittin/58.question: If the owner's willingness has to be read off a document, can any wording prove that he meant to sell rather than that he was still afraid?

gittin/59.question: If the reading order exists so that nobody has to judge who is greatest, what holds it up when the exception for Rav Huna depends on everyone agreeing that he was greatest?

gittin/62.question: Why should the husband's mistaken understanding of the messenger's role cancel the wife's own instruction, which the document in the end carried out?

gittin/69.question: Why should a mishna about which injured animals are doomed decide whether a sick person can still be healed?

gittin/71.question: If his gestures show the same clear mind in both marriages, why should the strength of the bond, rather than the clarity of what he means, decide whether he can end it?

gittin/74.question: If a court could rescue a seller from a buyer who hid on the last day, why is a wife left waiting on a husband who refuses to take her money?

gittin/78.question: When a rule says a woman is divorced but no one will rely on it until the document is in her hand, is she divorced?

gittin/79.question: If enclosure by walls is what delivers the document, so that it can fall nowhere but her place, is something given at the moment it can no longer go anywhere else, even though nothing ever reaches her hand?

gittin/80.question: If a divorce can survive the wrong kingdom's date but not a wrong name for the husband or wife, is what makes a document real the people it identifies rather than the power it honors?

gittin/82.question: Is a marriage a single bond that either ends or does not, or a bundle of prohibitions that can be lifted one man at a time?

gittin/84.question: Does a prohibition make an act impossible, or does it leave the act entirely possible and only attach a punishment to it?

kiddushin/3.question: The page rules that money claims cannot be learned from ritual ones, but why should a father's acknowledged power over his daughter's vows tell us nothing about his power over her money?

kiddushin/7.question: If a man's words are spoken in one breath and the woman agrees to all of them, why should naming her halves one at a time stop the betrothal from taking hold as a whole?

kiddushin/12.question: If a ruling can free a woman to marry another man and her children can still be treated as suspect, what has the ruling actually settled?

kiddushin/14.question: If reasoning could have overridden the verse about the Yom Kippur goats, what decides when a single limiting word is strong enough to stop an argument?

kiddushin/16.question: If puberty frees her because her body changed and she counts as a new person, why does her father's death, which ends his authority over her completely, leave her still a slave?

kiddushin/17.question: If the gift is owed only when the master's household prospered because of the slave, is it a share of profit earned or something the slave is owed simply for the six years themselves?

kiddushin/20.question: If the rule that a master not eat fine bread while his slave eats bran could not settle the price of the slave's freedom, what can such concern for him decide by itself?

kiddushin/26.question: If the hundred sheep never have to sit on the plot at all, why should handing over a tiny patch of land transfer them?

kiddushin/27.question: If the earth counts as one continuous thing even across ten countries, what stops a buyer who takes hold of one field from acquiring every field anywhere?

kiddushin/29.question: If a father may decide that his son's learning will not last and take the place of study for himself, is the duty owed to the son, or only to the Torah that someone in the house has to learn?

kiddushin/30.question: If Rav Yosef says his own generation cannot reproduce the count, why are the exact totals still passed on as settled facts?

kiddushin/32.question: If a teacher can give up the honor due him and still be owed the standing up, is that honor his to give away, or does it belong to the Torah he teaches?

kiddushin/33.question: If Abaye walks the long way around so nobody has to rise for him, what makes him call across the river to the rabbis who stayed seated: is the honor owed to him, or is it his to give up?

kiddushin/34.question: If a promise of long life is enough to keep women obligated in fixing a mezuza, does the reward attached to a commandment decide who is bound by it?

kiddushin/35.question: If a verse already settles that women are outside the prohibition against destroying the corners of the beard, why also offer the reason that women ordinarily have no beard, and does a rule still fit the woman its reason never described?

kiddushin/39.question: Is a promise still kept when the one who made it moves the payment to a world nobody has seen, or did Elisha ben Avuya read the fall correctly?

kiddushin/42.question: If no one can act as an agent for a sin because God's word outranks the sender's, what makes a word shared by two verses strong enough to set that reasoning aside?

kiddushin/43.question: When the court will not punish the man who sent the killer, what decides whether Heaven's judgment of him is the great one or the small one?

kiddushin/46.question: If both Rav and Shmuel agree the man knows the betrothal cannot take effect, what could ever settle whether the money he handed over without explanation was a deposit or a gift?

kiddushin/47.question: Once the page settles that she stays quiet only because he gave her almost the whole sum, why should her reluctance to ask for the rest decide whether he kept his terms, rather than the plain fact that he gave less than he said?

kiddushin/49.question: If an unspoken thought of repentance is enough to make the betrothal hold, why does the seller's unspoken plan to move to Eretz Yisrael count for nothing?

kiddushin/50.question: When a seller says out loud why he is selling, is the sale tied to that reason actually coming true, or only to his making the attempt?

kiddushin/53.question: If two opposite explanations fit the same two rulings equally well, what does a reason add to a ruling that already stands?

kiddushin/54.question: If a statement credited to Rabbi Meir can be handed over to Rabbi Yehuda whenever it clashes with the view assigned to him, what would ever count as evidence that Rabbi Meir held it?

kiddushin/55.question: If uncertainty about which offering the animal was can be covered by buying more animals and attaching conditions, how unlikely does a possibility have to be before it is simply waved away instead?

kiddushin/58.question: If the woman is betrothed to the agent anyway, what does calling his act deceitful take away from him?

kiddushin/59.question: If Ravin and Rav are excused for knowingly keeping what they were sent to get for someone else, while Rabbi Abba is asked to hand over a field he bought without knowing, does the wrong depend on what the taker knew or on what the other man lost?

kiddushin/60.question: If the betrothal counts from the moment he speaks even though the two hundred dinars may never arrive, is a person bound by what was promised or only by what was handed over?

kiddushin/64.question: If the father's word counts only where a verse grants it, why does the word of a man who would certainly know whether his own daughter was taken captive count for nothing there?

kiddushin/65.question: If their own admission is set aside because of the cost to relatives who never spoke, should a person's word about their own marriage ever be overridden by what it does to other people?

kiddushin/69.question: If a child takes the mother's status either way, why can a master's act of freeing wash slavery out of a family while nothing washes out the mamzer's flaw?

kiddushin/71.question: If the names are passed on so that nobody marries into such a family, why is telling them less often the better practice, when it leaves more people unwarned?

kiddushin/72.question: If Rav Yosef is glad of Rabbi Yosei's view because it keeps Elijah from exposing who the mamzerim are, is that view a claim about what is true or a decision about what can be borne?

kiddushin/75.question: If the same case can be read for the transgression, for the unfit sons, or for the unfit daughters, what decides which of those features is the real reason and which is an incidental detail?

kiddushin/76.question: If a man's lineage counts as clean because quarrels would already have exposed a flaw in it, does that make a family's fitness a matter of what is true about it or only of what its neighbors have said out loud?

kiddushin/77.question: If the child who did nothing carries the profaned status down the generations while the priest who chose the forbidden marriage is restored by a divorce, is that status a consequence of conduct at all, or only a fact about lineage?

kiddushin/82.question: If the world cannot exist without tanners, why does Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi pity the tanner rather than honor him for doing work everyone needs?

bava-kamma/3.question: If Rava can file pebbles under Trampling simply because that classification frees the owner from paying for damage in the street, why does Rav Pappa still need them to share something real with Trampling?

bava-kamma/7.question: If bran counts as payment of the best quality because some other city would buy it, is the injured party being paid in value or in the work of finding that buyer?

bava-kamma/8.question: If a buyer cannot give up this protection once another buyer would lose by it, why does a creditor's loss not count the same way?

bava-kamma/10.question: If the sixth man on the bench and the one who threw the bundle on the fire each turn out to have caused either everything or nothing, why is the man who deepened the pit by that last handbreadth counted as a partial cause rather than the same all-or-nothing?

bava-kamma/13.question: If dedicating the ox to the altar is what shrinks the amount the injured man can recover, should a person be able to lower what he owes by giving part of what he owns to God?

bava-kamma/14.question: If the same courtyard is the injured partner's ground for eating and like a public place for goring, does who owns it decide anything, or only what each partner was permitted to keep there?

bava-kamma/15.question: If no court in Babylonia will order the half payment, what makes the money his to keep once he seizes it himself?

bava-kamma/18.question: If nobody ever needed warning that a walking animal kicks up pebbles, can three warnings change what the owner owes, or does notice only matter for behavior that was a surprise in the first place?

bava-kamma/20.question: If living in the empty courtyard takes nothing from the owner, why does living under the consecrated beam count as taking something from the Temple?

bava-kamma/22.question: Rava's verse settles who pays, but if a wind did the carrying, in what sense is the blaze still the person's own force?

bava-kamma/23.question: Does a domain belong only to the ground a person owns, or can it travel around inside an animal's mouth wherever the animal walks?

bava-kamma/24.question: Does behaving abnormally cost you every claim against someone who then harms you, or only the claim you gave up by acting that way?

bava-kamma/25.question: If a rule can cut an argument down until it proves nothing, was that argument ever proof, or only a way of showing that the answer already written was the sensible one?

bava-kamma/26.question: If a sleeping man pays in full for vessels he never meant to break, why should the moment of the throw, rather than the broken jug on the floor, decide whether the thrower pays anything?

bava-kamma/27.question: If people ordinarily do not examine the road as they walk, why should a jug left there with permission turn that same walking into carelessness?

bava-kamma/29.question: If the stumbler goes free only because the fall was not his fault, why should one unlucky moment end his responsibility for shards that go on lying in the street?

bava-kamma/30.question: If the penalty really does hand the straw to whoever grabs it, can a law be real while the people who would act on it are kept from hearing it?

bava-kamma/31.question: If shouting a warning to the man behind is enough to free the fallen potter from paying for the broken pots, is the fault in lying across the road or in staying silent?

bava-kamma/32.question: If exile is the atonement for killing by accident, what is left for the man whose carelessness the page calls too great for exile?

bava-kamma/34.question: If the man who set the haystack alight on Shabbat owes nothing because he faces the death penalty, does the owner of the burned hay simply absorb the loss?

bava-kamma/38.question: If the verses already answer the objection, why is nothing said to the two officials who raise it, and can a rule be called just when its defense is offered only among the people it favors?

bava-kamma/39.question: Should a protection given to orphans give way whenever keeping it would discourage the very people willing to look after them?

bava-kamma/41.question: If three dead animals do not count as warning that an ox will kill a person, what is a record of past killings supposed to prove about the next one?

bava-kamma/43.question: When no atonement payment is possible at all, as with fire, is the victim's value still owed simply because a person died, or does that payment depend on the atonement it substitutes for?

bava-kamma/44.question: If ransom exists to atone for the owner and not to answer for the injury, does it make sense to sort obligations by whether money changes hands rather than by what the money is for?

bava-kamma/47.question: If merely saying yes makes a homeowner answer for a visitor's ox that strangles itself, how far does what he took on reach, and does it cover harm that arrives from outside his courtyard?

bava-kamma/49.question: If the money for the miscarried offspring belongs to the husband alone, so that his death with no heirs leaves the man who caused the harm holding it, what makes those offspring his and not hers?

bava-kamma/50.question: If a fall of six handbreadths crushes an ox badly enough that Rav Naḥman forbids eating its meat, why does the digger of that shallow channel owe nothing for the animal that died in it?

bava-kamma/54.question: If an ox's failure to watch where it walked cancels the payment entirely, why does the person who left an open pit in the road carry none of the loss at all?

bava-kamma/55.question: If no court will ever collect it, in what sense does the man who breaks the fence owe the animal's owner anything?

bava-kamma/56.question: If no court will ever collect from these four, what changes for a person told he still owes the loss?

bava-kamma/57.question: If the doubled payment falls on the thief because he fears people and not Heaven, why should the owner, whose loss is the same either way, be paid twice by one taker and once by the other?

bava-kamma/59.question: Should a person pay for what he destroyed as it stood at that moment, or for what it would have become if he had left it alone?

bava-kamma/60.question: If burning another man's barley to save your own life is forbidden to everyone else, does the king's permission make the act right, or only make it unpunishable?

bava-kamma/61.question: If a fire's reach is measured by how large it was when lit, is the one who kindled it paying for what he did or for what he should have expected?

bava-kamma/67.question: If the one case where a new and permanent name fails to make a new thing is explained away as a leniency, what is left to show that naming ever changes what a thing is?

bava-kamma/68.question: If a sale that transfers nothing still costs a kidnapper his life, why should a thief's equally empty sale of an ox cost him nothing?

bava-kamma/70.question: Why should it matter that one pair's account could stand by itself, when neither pair actually saw the man both take the ox and kill it?

bava-kamma/71.question: If the thief who is executed still owes the owner four or five oxen even though no court will ever collect that money, what makes the debt real?

bava-kamma/72.question: If the Torah simply declares the second pair credible without giving a reason, why should that strangeness be a reason to let the liar's other testimony stand until the day he was caught?

bava-kamma/75.question: If a confession only frees a thief from the fines when it also commits him to repay the animal's value, is he being spared for telling the truth or for agreeing to lose money?

bava-kamma/78.question: Is a thief who keeps the unborn calf holding back part of the animal he sold, when that calf will separate from its mother on its own?

bava-kamma/79.question: If the thief is penalized precisely for minding what people think of him, why does the same sage credit his embarrassment at carrying a sheep and lower the fine?

bava-kamma/81.question: If the same broad steps look like showing off from a stranger and devotion from a known student, how can anyone tell whether a man who declines a right Joshua granted is aiming at Heaven or at being seen?

bava-kamma/82.question: If nine of Jerusalem's rules come with a reason and the tenth is kept only because it was handed down, is the tenth the weakest of the ten or the firmest?

bava-kamma/86.question: If nothing more can be taken from the imbecile's standing, is honor something a person is paid for only while he still has some left to lose?

bava-kamma/87.question: Why should the answer to who keeps the compensation turn on how particular a given father is, rather than on one rule that holds for every father?

bava-kamma/88.question: If keeping most of the commandments makes a slave a brother for the insult done to him, why should one missing word in a verse settle that his word in court counts for nothing?

bava-kamma/91.question: If the same uncovering shames a woman whether she does it or a stranger does, does the wrong lie in what happened to her or in who chose it?

bava-kamma/92.question: If paying in full does not settle the matter until the victim forgives, why may a person sign away his jug in advance but not his own eye?

bava-kamma/93.question: If a man may give up payment for his own pain but not for a lost limb because his family carries the shame, why should relatives who never spoke outweigh the word he gave himself?

bava-kamma/96.question: If Rav Naḥman grants that the rule frees the robber from paying for the field's increase, can a judge charge him anyway because of the kind of man he is?

bava-kamma/97.question: If the free labor costs the owner nothing, why does it become forbidden once the man taking it is the owner's creditor and it only looks like interest?

bava-kamma/98.question: Once the page settles that deafening changes the body while the hammer leaves the coin its full size, why does Rabba still have to add that most cows never become offerings, and is a thing harmed when only its worth drops and not its substance?

bava-kamma/99.question: If handing the butcher a coin before he starts is what makes him owe for the animal he ruins, is care owed to the work itself or only to whoever paid for it?

bava-kamma/102.question: If an agent who follows instructions counts as the buyer's own hand, why should buying barley instead of wheat make the grain the agent's own property rather than a bad purchase he simply owes for?

bava-kamma/103.question: If the pious man swore no false oath and robbed no one, on what grounds is he made to pay two men for one purchase?

bava-kamma/104.question: When someone names a messenger in front of witnesses, does that make the messenger an extension of the one who named him, or only a name the other side may choose to trust at his own risk?

bava-kamma/105.question: If a remainder too small to count still keeps an act from being finished, why can Rava decide that for the bundles and the hairs but not for the half sealed hole?

bava-kamma/108.question: Does the bailee lose the owner's trust when he speaks the false oath, or already when he decides to swear it?

bava-kamma/109.question: If a robbery debt can be cancelled when the person owed is someone else, why should cancelling it fail when the one owed and the one who owes are the same man?

bava-kamma/110.question: If the man who was robbed is dead and the money reaches the priests as a gift rather than as his inheritance, whom is the robber actually repaying?

bava-kamma/112.question: If witnesses about to sail overseas can be heard without the defendant present, why should Rabbi Yirmeya's witnesses wait years for a child to grow up before anyone tests his claim to the chamber?

bava-kamma/113.question: If crooked judging is barred only because God's name would be desecrated, does that make the crookedness wrong only where someone can see it?

bava-kamma/116.question: Is the rescuer paid for what he gave up or for what he accomplished, when Rav pays him in full though he lost nothing and Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi pays only a wage though he lost his own donkey?

bava-metzia/2.question: If the only way to keep both oaths honest is to picture the two men lifting the garment at the same moment, is the court using the oath to find the truth or to make its division look clean?

bava-metzia/4.question: If the oath of the two men holding a garment really is the Sages' own invention, does a rule they make need an older rule in the Torah to imitate, or can they simply make it?

bava-metzia/5.question: If a bailee's oath is trusted because he never realized that paying for what he kept was still wrong, is a person's honesty measured by what he did or by what he believed he was doing?

bava-metzia/8.question: If two deaf-mutes own what they lift only because the Sages wanted to prevent a quarrel, is ownership a fact about who took the item, or a convenience handed out wherever a fight seems likely?

bava-metzia/12.question: If the poor are repaid only by what their own sons may gather years later, have they agreed to give up their stalks, or just been told they will come out even?

bava-metzia/13.question: If two people's agreement about a debt can be a conspiracy against the buyers who are not in the room, what lets Shmuel treat that same agreement as simply true?

bava-metzia/16.question: If the sale of a field the seller did not own takes effect only because the buyer relied on him to make it good, is the seller bound by his own word or by another man's confidence in him?

bava-metzia/18.question: When two men in one town can share a name, does a written document identify the people it names, or only the accidental marks on the paper that no other copy has?

bava-metzia/20.question: If a creditor's own signed writing proves nothing about payment while the pile of torn papers he threw it into proves it, is a person's real intent better read from what he writes or from what he throws away?

bava-metzia/22.question: If the fallen dates may be eaten because everyone knows creeping creatures will get to them, is the owner's giving up something he actually did, or only what a finder assumes any owner would have done?

bava-metzia/23.question: If a vessel with no identifying mark is handed to a Torah scholar because he says he recognizes it, why should his word be trusted when the same passage permits Sages to say what is not true about three matters?

bava-metzia/24.question: If the law already lets the finder keep the purse, what sort of claim is Shmuel answering when he gives it back to an owner who can describe it?

bava-metzia/28.question: If Rabba bar Rav Huna can decide that the witnesses meant the opposite of what they said, on the reasoning that nobody brings witnesses to condemn himself, what is left of testimony as the words a witness actually speaks?

bava-metzia/32.question: If an animal is suffering right now and a person's own hatred could be worn down instead, why should the work on the self come first?

bava-metzia/35.question: If paying without being taken to court is what would have given the friend the found jewels and their increase, is that gain earned by his conduct or granted by the owner's goodwill?

bava-metzia/36.question: If the second man guards the cow just as carefully, is the owner really harmed by the fact that only a stranger, and not the man he chose, can now swear to what happened?

bava-metzia/38.question: If the wine is beyond saving and only the empty casks can still be rescued, is the keeper still returning a lost item to the owner, or does acting on someone's behalf make sense only while the thing they left can still be saved?

bava-metzia/40.question: If the fixed rate applies only where nobody can measure what was actually lost, is it stating what grain really loses over a year, or only setting a price for not knowing?

bava-metzia/41.question: When the use left the animal exactly as it was, is the bailee paying for harm he caused or for having treated another person's property as his own?

bava-metzia/46.question: If a coin the king banned still passes from hand to hand in private, and a coin one province rejected still spends elsewhere, what makes either of them stop counting as money?

bava-metzia/50.question: If cancelling a whole sale was uncommon enough for the Gemara to set it aside in one argument, why would a full day to cancel frighten the merchants of Lod more than handing back every overcharge?

bava-metzia/52.question: If a hole in the middle of a worn coin ends the fear of deceit and a hole at the edge does not, is a thing made harmless by what was done to it or by what someone could still do with it?

bava-metzia/53.question: Does a quantity too small to be redeemed lose its holiness, or keep it with no way left to act on it?

bava-metzia/55.question: If the Temple must be repaid for misuse worth less than a peruta, why should an ordinary person robbed of that same amount be owed nothing?

bava-metzia/56.question: Does sowing wheat kernels into a field change what they are, or only where they are?

bava-metzia/57.question: If no one may redeem a hundred dinars of Temple goods onto one peruta to begin with, what does it mean that the redemption holds anyway once it is done?

bava-metzia/66.question: If the case is decided by whether the borrower refuses to sell his other land cheaply, why should an outward sign of financial ease stand in for what he actually meant when he promised the field?

bava-metzia/67.question: If a court will never make the lender give the crops back, in what sense is eating them forbidden?

bava-metzia/69.question: The page says a judge must give his reasons where there is room for suspicion, so if it took the loser's complaint to pull the explanation out, what happens to the rulings nobody complains about?

bava-metzia/70.question: If terms that shield an investor from loss make an adult wicked but are the chosen way to preserve an orphan's inheritance, is the arrangement wrong in itself or only wrong for someone free to choose otherwise?

bava-metzia/76.question: If the laborers who agreed to three dinars are owed no money yet still have a complaint, was the wage they accepted fair, or only enforceable?

bava-metzia/78.question: If Rabba can already explain the payment by a snake that was just as likely on either road, what changes once Rabbi Yoḥanan names the renter a robber for breaking his word?

bava-metzia/80.question: Why does a buyer's disbelief cancel the sale when the seller pads the list with faults the cow does not have, but not when the seller leaves the rest of the list vague?

bava-metzia/81.question: If a ruling turns out to be correct only because of a fact nobody knew when it was given, was the judge right to give it?

bava-metzia/82.question: If a barrel broken on flat ground already looks like carelessness, what would a man have to show for the break to count as an accident he could honestly swear to?

bava-metzia/83.question: When Rav answers that returning the cloaks and paying the wages is the law, and his source is a verse about walking in the way of good men, is he collecting a debt or compelling a kindness?

bava-metzia/86.question: If heaven could take Rabba only in the moment he chose death over arrest by the king, was he summoned or was he cornered?

bava-metzia/91.question: If lashes answer to God and money answers to the cow's owner, has one act of muzzling become two separate wrongs, or one wrong counted twice?

bava-metzia/93.question: Does paying a person to watch something raise what may be demanded of him above what everyone else does, or does a wage buy only ordinary care with the costs passed back?

bava-metzia/95.question: If a single moment of the owner's service when the cow changes hands cancels the borrower's payment even though the owner is absent when the animal dies, why should the start of an arrangement decide more than what is happening at the moment the loss occurs?

bava-metzia/97.question: If who is lent to whom turns on who picks the tractate, why does Rava's teaching count for less than the help his students give his own learning?

bava-metzia/99.question: If the neighbor is paid only what the lump was worth as it sat, why is the Temple treasury paid what the dates could have fetched one at a time?

bava-metzia/100.question: When Rava saves Sumakhos's rule by deciding that the seller and buyer must have said "perhaps", is he showing what the mishna meant or shielding a rule the mishna's plain words contradict?

bava-metzia/106.question: Can an owner charge a tenant for the good fortune his own merit might have brought, when the page cannot say who was worthy of a miracle?

bava-metzia/108.question: If a verse about doing what is right and good can take a purchased field away from a buyer who broke no law, why does the curse of the tree owner, who was only using a right the page grants him, still take effect?

bava-metzia/109.question: If Rava says the land itself did half the growing, why is the departing planter paid anything at all for it, while Rav Pappa, whose palm trees also came up on their own, gets only firewood value?

bava-metzia/112.question: If the laborer's need to eat was reason enough to move the oath from the employer onto him, why does the page abandon that reason and rest the rule instead on a guess about which of the two is more likely to have forgotten?

bava-metzia/113.question: Rav Ḥagga's objection is left hanging when the page breaks off in the middle of the reply to it: why should the man who is owed money be the one made responsible for keeping the debtor fed and rested?

bava-metzia/114.question: If he threw the leaves away the moment he heard the voice, can a benefit already soaked into his cloak be given back, or only passed on to someone else?

bava-metzia/117.question: If the water sits on the floor a moment before it finds the hole, at what point does the man who poured it stop being the one who shot the arrow?

bava-batra/2.question: If the roof must be walled off because the neighbor cannot know when he is being watched, is the harm in being seen, or in not knowing?

bava-batra/3.question: If the worry is that a synagogue once torn down may never be rebuilt, why does a crack in the wall settle that worry instead of sharpening it?

bava-batra/6.question: If being seen by passersby who happen to look up counts for less than being seen by the neighbor opposite, is the harm in the seeing itself or in living under a steady watch?

bava-batra/7.question: Why should inheriting from the same father leave a brother with less protection for his light than a stranger has for a room holding only straw and wood?

bava-batra/8.question: If hunger was enough to feed one man but not to change the rule, and only the risk of turning away a hidden scholar opened the storehouses to everyone, what is the food being given for?

bava-batra/10.question: If the king's order to starve the prisoner is the same in both parables, why should feeding a son count as obedience and feeding a slave count as defiance?

bava-batra/13.question: If having no money lets one owner refuse the larger share of the courtyard, why does having no money still leave the poor brother free to demand that the rich one buy him out?

bava-batra/15.question: If a name and a hometown are enough to prove Job was a real man rather than a parable, what does it mean that the sages cannot agree within a thousand years about when he lived?

bava-batra/18.question: If Ravina makes the buyer move the harmful thing even though he placed it lawfully, does staying within the rules protect a person from anything?

bava-batra/19.question: Is the straw part of the window because its owner has stopped wanting it, or only because nobody anywhere could still find a use for it?

bava-batra/23.question: If Rav Yosef can make crows into smoke by declaring himself sensitive, what keeps every neighbor from setting the threshold at his own nerves?

bava-batra/24.question: Is a guess about how thieves behave a stronger reason to permit the wine than a count of how many vineyards in the area are not orla?

bava-batra/25.question: If the Divine Presence is everywhere, what makes the west too holy for a tannery, and why would any other side be less so?

bava-batra/27.question: If a tree's roots feed on a neighbor's land, is the fruit stolen, or did Joshua's apportioning of the land settle in advance that nobody may complain?

bava-batra/28.question: If alfalfa cut in snatches fails because that is not how a field is normally worked, is what proves ownership the count of three at all, or the sight of someone using land the way an owner would?

bava-batra/29.question: If the three years only mean that a buyer has stopped keeping his deed, is it fair to hold him to a protest he never heard, on the assumption that gossip must have reached him?

bava-batra/30.question: If a man forfeits his claim by signing for the buyer's benefit but keeps it after telling the buyer to go buy the field, does a person answer for what he did more than for what another person relied on?

bava-batra/31.question: If a court can take back land it has already awarded once new witnesses arrive, why is a woman who already remarried left in her marriage when witnesses arrive saying her first husband lives?

bava-batra/37.question: If the tree owner's claim to any ground comes only from the threat that his trees could be ordered uprooted, why should that threat buy him half the field rather than just the earth his roots need?

bava-batra/38.question: If Rav is right that word travels from friend to friend to friend, does a protest count from the moment it is spoken, or only once there is a real path for it to reach the man working the field?

bava-batra/40.question: If a court can read the coercion straight off the woman's ultimatum with no declaration filed beforehand, why should witnesses ever have to put in writing that they know the pressure a seller was under?

bava-batra/43.question: If a benefit shared by every resident makes each of them a biased witness, who in that town is left who can testify?

bava-batra/44.question: When a seller's testimony would mainly help his creditor collect a debt, is that enough of a gain to himself to make him an interested witness?

bava-batra/46.question: If the owner only wins once he has seen the cloak, and Rav Ashi shows him how to make the craftsman produce it, does the law here decide who owns the cloak or who argues better?

bava-batra/48.question: If a sale stands even when the buyer named the one field and the seller chose nothing at all, what is left of the claim that being coerced makes a man decide he wants to sell?

bava-batra/49.question: If her claim that she signed only to please her husband covers just three fields tied to her marriage contract, why does that same wish to please not undo her signature on everything else she owns?

bava-batra/51.question: If sages can decide that a document saying "sold" really means gift because that is what the husband must have wanted, what is left of the words a person chooses to write?

bava-batra/54.question: Mar Ukva settles the case by pointing to what people usually do, so is land won by what a person meant to accomplish, as Shmuel's tests assume, or only by acts that others already recognize as owning?

bava-batra/58.question: Did the son who refused to beat his father's grave prove that he was the son, or only that he was decent?

bava-batra/61.question: If the boundaries written in a deed only show roughly where the property sits, is a document binding for what its words say or for what the seller probably meant?

bava-batra/64.question: When a contract is silent, whose unspoken assumption should govern: the buyer who does not want strangers walking through the house he just paid for, or the seller who would otherwise have to fly through the air to reach his own pit?

bava-batra/65.question: Why should a brother's wish to live as his ancestors lived count as a claim on his brother's land, when a buyer who paid money for the same house gets no such right?

bava-batra/66.question: If the pipe counts as a vessel now only because it was one before it was set into the ground, does what a thing once was decide what it is now?

bava-batra/70.question: Why is a dead father's silence toward his children treated as proof that he never repaid, when the document still sitting in the depositor's hands was ruled to prove nothing?

bava-batra/71.question: If a giver is presumed to mean everything he owns, can the figure he himself stated, 100 barrels, ever limit what he gave?

bava-batra/72.question: If a ruling recorded in Rabbi Shimon's name turns out to be an argument made inside the Rabbis' premise rather than his own view, how is a reader supposed to tell which of his other rulings he actually holds?

bava-batra/75.question: Is the student destroyed for doubting his teacher, or for needing proof before believing him, and can someone who believes only what he has seen be said to trust anyone at all?

bava-batra/79.question: Once the page assumes that a person consecrating means the widest gift he could have meant, what is left of the words he actually said?

bava-batra/80.question: When a ruling can be fitted to Rabbi Eliezer only by reading its words as their opposite, is it still that ruling being explained, or a new one being written?

bava-batra/82.question: If buying the third tree wins a man his own patch of ground but costs him the right to walk across the field to reach it, is owning a thing outright worth less than holding it inside someone else's property?

bava-batra/83.question: If whether you can sow between them is not what decides, what makes a tree important enough to pull the ground into the sale when a thorny shrub is not?

bava-batra/89.question: The page reports that he taught them anyway, so does spelling out exactly how a measure is rigged protect buyers more than it arms sellers?

bava-batra/90.question: If a seller is judged by what his holding back does to the whole year's prices, why should growing the produce yourself make holding it back allowed?

bava-batra/91.question: If Elimelech's punishment came from staying silent rather than from leaving, what is left to prove that leaving was wrong, and is a leader answerable for where he lives or for what he asks on behalf of others?

bava-batra/92.question: If most buyers of an ox want it for plowing, why should that fact be strong enough to decide a ritual question but too weak to decide who keeps the money?

bava-batra/94.question: If no one can tell whether the seller mixed the extra dirt in or it got there during processing, can a penalty be imposed on suspicion alone?

bava-batra/95.question: If thirty slivers of extra land count as one plot because they can be added together, why can the dirt spread through a batch of produce never add up to a thing of its own?

bava-batra/97.question: If a foul wine is barred because no governor would accept such a gift, why do the other inferior wines still count once they have already been poured?

bava-batra/100.question: If a vineyard path becomes yours by walking because walking is the only use it has, is land owned by whoever uses it for what it exists for?

bava-batra/101.question: Is a plan that fits only once the corner niches are said to hold non-viable newborns an answer to the problem, or a quiet admission that the chamber cannot hold what it was drawn to hold?

bava-batra/102.question: If the hastily buried body was never actually moved, why does the plan to move it count for more than the vineyard owner's plan to uproot the vines that fail?

bava-batra/103.question: If appearance to the buyer is what keeps the deep crevices out of the measurement, why can the page not say whether rocks set in a ring or a row make one field look like two?

bava-batra/105.question: When a contract's second clause says something the first does not, is that a speaker changing his terms, as Rav treats it, or a speaker whose meaning nobody can recover, so that the money simply stays where it already sits?

bava-batra/106.question: If a stated twenty se'a can be reread as praise of a field's fruitfulness rather than a claim about its size, what could a seller say that a buyer would be entitled to rely on?

bava-batra/108.question: If the verse names a son's inheritance first, why should a teacher's fondness for a rule he had to derive set the order of a legal list?

bava-batra/110.question: If Jonathan's love of money was obvious enough for David to notice, what made it a reason to trust him with the Temple treasuries rather than to keep him far from them?

bava-batra/111.question: If it took three derivations, the first two undone by further cases, to rule out a firstborn's double portion from his mother's property, what made that question one worth dismissing as not asked in order to learn?

bava-batra/112.question: Does an assumption about where a righteous man could be buried settle a question of inheritance law, or does it only show what the arguers could not bring themselves to picture?

bava-batra/113.question: If handing out an estate counts as an act of judgment, is a dying man's property given away by his own word or only by a court's ruling?

bava-batra/115.question: If the dispute is only about a daughter sharing the estate with her brother's daughter, what does a verse calling a grandson a son prove against the old man?

bava-batra/118.question: Does Joshua's advice to hide in the forests still hold for people who say the evil eye has no power over them?

bava-batra/119.question: If the generation that died in the wilderness really held the land and yet never inherited it, what is left of owning a thing you can only hand on?

bava-batra/122.question: If Elazar announces the pairing before his hand goes into the box, is the lottery still a lottery, or is it there so the people watching can see the announcement come true?

bava-batra/123.question: If Leah's prayers first earned the birthright and Rachel's silence later took it back, what makes one sister's claim on it stronger than the other's?

bava-batra/124.question: If a thickened palm tree still counts as the father's but grain that has filled out into ears may not, when has a thing merely grown and when has it become something else?

bava-batra/133.question: If the law lets a father hand everything to strangers and the Sages answer only with displeasure, does a son have a claim on his father's property or merely an expectation his father may end?

bava-batra/135.question: Does Rava, who never gives up his resolution, now think the widow is genuinely forbidden to remarry, or only that a court may not say she is permitted?

bava-batra/137.question: If the sale stands even though advising it is called wicked, what does the second person's claim amount to while the first is still alive?

bava-batra/139.question: Why should the widow's loss count against the husband while the buyers' loss does not, when the only difference named is that the buyers could have seen it coming?

bava-batra/141.question: When a recorded mishna contradicts a rule, is it fair for Rav Huna to set the text aside as unattributable, or should the rule give way to the text?

bava-batra/145.question: If the extra is not interest because it came out of joy, why can a man who was never told about the wedding, and shared in none of that joy, still be made to pay in court?

bava-batra/146.question: If presents are kept or returned according to whether they are the kind that get eaten rather than according to what they cost, is a gift measured by its value or by whether it can still be handed back?

bava-batra/147.question: If the rule was invented only to keep a dying man from being tormented by seeing his wishes ignored, why should his spoken gift then hold as firmly as one the Torah itself commands?

bava-batra/148.question: If the law is willing to assume a dying man quietly kept back some land in another province, why does it stay open whether the man who gave everything to the poor really meant to part with all of it?

bava-batra/150.question: If the two categories are property that has to be carried and land that stays where it is, can a slave who walks on his own honestly be either one?

bava-batra/152.question: When a giver adds a formal gesture to a deed he has already written, does the extra step make his gift firmer, or admit that the deed alone was never meant to bind?

bava-batra/158.question: If no one can prove which of them died first, why should keeping land inside the mother's tribe count for more than splitting it between two sets of heirs with equal claims?

bava-batra/165.question: The page calls his answer fitting whichever version was really asked, but can an answer be judged good once no one can say what it was answering?

bava-batra/169.question: When the agent is ordered to become the seller and stand behind the guarantee with his own property, is that fixing the deal he botched or making him pay for it?

bava-batra/170.question: Once the amount owed has changed, why should only a court be trusted to write the replacement note, and why should that note carry the date of the old one?

bava-batra/171.question: When either side can be cheated by a lost piece of paper, is "the borrower is a servant to the lender" a reason for putting the risk on the debtor, or only a description of how things already are?

bava-batra/175.question: If what binds a guarantor is the creditor's reliance at the moment he hands over the money, why should the debtor's release from being strangled count for nothing?

sanhedrin/2.question: If a person can be acquitted by a single vote but convicted only by two, is that extra vote a claim about the evidence or about which mistake a court can bear to make?

sanhedrin/3.question: If three judges are required only because one of them will probably turn out to be learned, does the panel actually protect the person being judged, or does it only make a wrong ruling less likely?

sanhedrin/4.question: If the same consonants can be read two ways, is the Torah the letters that were written down or the sounds that were passed along with them?

sanhedrin/8.question: Can one person both carry a people the way a nursing father carries an infant and strike them upon their skulls, or does being the only leader make the first impossible?

sanhedrin/9.question: Should the worry that killers go untried be allowed to decide who counts as a witness?

sanhedrin/11.question: The divorce documents left the woman free to marry, but she still never learned which man had betrothed her, so does she have a claim to know his name even when sparing him public shame means hiding it?

sanhedrin/12.question: If Hezekiah's added month still held as valid, does a ruler who decided by the best count he had owe anyone an apology once the count turns out wrong?

sanhedrin/14.question: If being ordained could get a man killed, why is the same honor worth Rabbi Yoḥanan's grief when he cannot give it and worth a wedding song when it is given?

sanhedrin/15.question: If hair ready to be shorn stays part of the body because waiting makes it worth more, is a thing judged by what it is now or by the direction its value is moving?

sanhedrin/19.question: When a rule is made because the court was too frightened to enforce the law against a powerful man, is it still a statement about what is right, or only a record of who had the power?

sanhedrin/21.question: If Solomon fell by deciding he could marry many wives and still keep his heart from turning, what separates that reasoning from Rabbi Yehuda's permission, which rests on the same stated reason?

sanhedrin/26.question: When a lawful reason for working the field is available and might be true, is the man plowing judged by that reason or by what he actually intends?

sanhedrin/27.question: When bar Ḥama walks free and takes on Rav Pappi's tax for all of his years, is that gratitude or a payment, and why does the page report it without comment?

sanhedrin/28.question: If a sense of affinity is enough to bar a man from testifying about the woman he is betrothed to, why does that same affinity count for nothing between the father of the groom and the father of the bride?

sanhedrin/30.question: If the document can announce that the judges disagreed without saying who disagreed, what makes attaching a name to the dissent gossip rather than plain accuracy?

sanhedrin/31.question: If late proof is accepted from someone presumed not to have known about it and refused from someone presumed to have held it back, is the court judging the proof or the person who brings it?

sanhedrin/32.question: Can a court make itself more merciful by choosing which sentence it speaks first?

sanhedrin/33.question: The page says the loss came from the owner's own act of feeding the cow to the dogs, but should a person who acts on a recognized expert's mistaken ruling be counted as the cause of his own loss?

sanhedrin/34.question: If one of the two derivations is known to be wrong but nobody can say which, why does the acquittal still count as a vote at all?

sanhedrin/36.question: If a court expects that junior judges will never contradict a senior who has already spoken, why trust the opinions they give when they speak first?

sanhedrin/40.question: If the seven questions are kept partly to confuse the witnesses rather than to learn what happened, why should an accused man go free because a witness could not name the seven-year cycle?

sanhedrin/41.question: If witnesses have already warned him and he acted anyway, what does the court gain by also requiring him to say in his own words that he knows the act will cost him his life?

sanhedrin/42.question: If the court's own good name is what keeps the deliberations going and the walk to the stoning ground long, is the chance to save the condemned man only a side effect of that concern?

sanhedrin/45.question: If one verse about loving your neighbor can make both stripping a condemned person and clothing them the kinder death, who is fit to decide which one he would have wanted?

sanhedrin/46.question: If no verse can be found that requires burying the dead at all, does it still matter whether burial removes disgrace or brings atonement?

sanhedrin/47.question: If being killed unjustly wipes away sin with no repentance at all, why should a death the court judged deserved leave the sin standing?

sanhedrin/48.question: Once the ruling is that only actual use forbids an object, is a thing kept out of ordinary hands because of what it truly is, or because of what people watching would take it to be?

sanhedrin/51.question: If, as Rav Yosef finally says, the four readings of Rabbi Eliezer's line differ only in wording and not in anything a court would do, why does it matter which one is called the law?

sanhedrin/52.question: Once the verse about loving your neighbor has been limited to picking the least painful way of burning a person, what stops that same concern from reaching the decision to burn him at all?

sanhedrin/53.question: If a murderer may be killed by any method available once he is about to escape, what is the Torah's assigned method of execution protecting when he is not?

sanhedrin/54.question: If the animal is killed so that no one in the marketplace will point at it and recall how the man died, what does a man the court has already executed still have that the law protects?

sanhedrin/55.question: If living animals are spared out of pity, is the stoned animal killed for having enjoyed the act, or only for the shame a person would carry from seeing it alive?

sanhedrin/65.question: If Rava has to move the crime of the lying witnesses from their voice to their sight in order to keep it out of the category of action, where does their wrongdoing actually sit?

sanhedrin/66.question: If forbidding the curse of an ordinary parent depends on calling the words about judges unnecessary, does the prohibition rest on anything about the parent himself?

sanhedrin/69.question: If bodies in earlier generations could do at eight what bodies now cannot, should a law be built on what people once could do or on what they can do today?

sanhedrin/70.question: Why should a boy who breaks God's food laws fall outside a punishment that still reaches the boy whose only defiance was of his parents?

sanhedrin/72.question: Why would Rava refuse his own rams on the strength of a ruling he had argued against, and can a person hold himself bound by a law he thinks is wrong?

sanhedrin/73.question: Can a degradation be ranked as great or small by the punishment attached to it, when the person degraded might rank it otherwise?

sanhedrin/74.question: If a gentile's own pleasure already excuses the act, what is Abaye adding by calling Esther passive, and can someone who only submits be said to have transgressed at all?

sanhedrin/76.question: If a man who holds another under water until he drowns is a murderer though he struck no blow, why is the man who sets a snake on him only the cause of a death?

sanhedrin/78.question: If the amount of life a victim has left decides whether his killer is executed, is the killer being judged for what he did or for what was left to take?

sanhedrin/79.question: If a man who intended murder and committed murder owes neither his life nor a payment, is the crime measured by what his hand did or by the name he spoke first?

sanhedrin/83.question: If the difference between death at the hand of Heaven and karet comes down to whether one word stands in the plural or the singular, is that a reason or only a resemblance?

sanhedrin/84.question: The page explains Rav's refusal as fear of an unintended wound, so does a permission to injure in order to heal cover only the hand that does not slip, and not the mistakes that healing always risks?

sanhedrin/86.question: If being in someone's keeping means a child cannot be stolen from it, what protects the pupils of a teacher who decides to sell them?

sanhedrin/90.question: Does a verse prove resurrection because of what it says, or only because nobody in the room could offer another reading of it?

sanhedrin/92.question: Why does a pair of inherited prayer boxes count as an argument in a dispute otherwise settled by quoting verses?

sanhedrin/93.question: The page gives two reasons Joshua came out scorched, the wicked men burning next to him and a fault of his own, so is a person damaged by the company he is thrown in with or only by what he himself failed to do?

sanhedrin/102.question: If Manasseh knew a law Rav Ashi did not, and claims that anyone alive in his day would have chased idols, does that plea excuse him, or is it precisely why he is denied a share in the World-to-Come?

sanhedrin/103.question: If feeding travelers was enough to protect the man who made the idol, why was the same idol counted against the soldiers who only failed to tear it down?

sanhedrin/106.question: If God is willing to leave Doeg one small thing and David is not, whose measure of a learned wicked man does the page end up accepting?

sanhedrin/107.question: If the rule that one who makes the masses sin cannot repent is a true teaching, why does the page blame the teachers rather than the students who believed it?

makkot/2.question: When a verse and a reason point in opposite directions, as they do over exile here, why should the verse decide while the reason is left standing and unanswered?

makkot/4.question: If the only two cases where words alone bring lashes are each exceptional in their own way, what would a case have to look like before Rabbi Yehuda would call it too strange to learn a general rule from?

makkot/10.question: If the fall from the ladder was arranged so that each man would finally get what he deserved, is the one who fell being punished for the death he just caused or for the earlier killing nobody saw?

makkot/13.question: If Rabbi Meir proves the office comes back from a verse about a freed slave, what makes a position of honor a man's own rather than something his town lent him?

makkot/14.question: If Reish Lakish cannot use the linked verses because no teacher passed that link to him, is a derivation that must be received rather than worked out a real proof?

makkot/15.question: If writing an extra positive command next to a prohibition cannot make that prohibition less severe, why should a command built into it remove the lashes entirely?

makkot/16.question: If Rav Aḥa's vow was meant to protect the children from a teacher who neglected them, why does putting that same teacher back in front of them count as the kind of commandment that dissolves such a vow?

makkot/17.question: If every one of Rabbi Shimon's comparisons can be refuted, does the flogging he derived from them keep its force?

makkot/18.question: Why should flesh that no one at all may eat draw fewer prohibitions than flesh a priest could lawfully have eaten?

makkot/20.question: If the man whose head another person shaved is flogged only once he tilts his head to help, is the lash for the bare corner or for the helping?

makkot/22.question: If the attendant who kills a man while striking the count the court ordered owes nothing for that death, what changes at the one extra lash that makes him a killer who must flee?

shevuot/2.question: If a shared general purpose lets the goats be exchanged, what is left of Rabbi Shimon's insistence that each one atones for something different?

shevuot/5.question: If the offering is owed because a man once touched something impure and could have drawn the conclusion from a lesson learned in childhood, is he answerable for what he knew or for what he failed to think about?

shevuot/6.question: Akiva makes naming the shades the condition for ruling on them, so what does a name give a priest that careful looking does not?

shevuot/9.question: If a goat can atone for God's diminishing of the moon, is that an admission that the act was wrong, or only an expression of regret for it?

shevuot/12.question: If the law itself would let the recovered goat brought to atone for sin be burned on the altar like the surplus lambs, why should the risk that a bystander mistakes it decide the case?

shevuot/17.question: If hastening a fire that would have burned anyway counts as doing the service, when is a person the one who did a thing rather than the one who made it happen sooner?

shevuot/18.question: If waiting is blameless and pulling away at once is a transgression, is the man being judged for what he did or for how much he enjoyed it?

shevuot/19.question: If nothing a person does afterward can show which of the two things he had forgotten, can a rule that turns on the contents of his mind ever be applied to him?

shevuot/22.question: When a man swears off something nobody eats, should his words be measured by what eating normally means, or by what he must have meant?

shevuot/24.question: If the grapes are what let the second oath take hold, why should the figs, already forbidden by the first oath, become forbidden all over again?

shevuot/27.question: If an oath binds only when the opposite oath could also have been sworn, is a promise to keep a commandment worth less than a promise about an optional act?

shevuot/29.question: If an oath is measured by the court's understanding and not by the swearer's own meaning, is the man bound by something he chose, or only by the words he happened to say?

shevuot/32.question: If the two men already know why the plaintiff is chasing them, why should their oath become a wrong only once he has said the words out loud?

shevuot/35.question: If a word counts as God's name only when nothing else in the world answers to it, is the swearer bound by what he meant or by what his words could mean?

shevuot/37.question: If the page finally decides that a denial witnesses stand ready to disprove still counts as a denial, what makes a lie that could never have worked into a sin that needs an offering?

shevuot/38.question: If the Gemara would sooner say the whole mishna belongs to someone other than Rabbi Meir than accept Rabbi Yoḥanan's reading of him, what makes a sage's stated view worth more protection than the text that reports it?

shevuot/40.question: If the court already assumes that a man denying his whole debt may only be delaying payment, what is his oath supposed to settle?

shevuot/42.question: What do Abaye and Rava see in that one sentence, spoken before the loan went wrong, that makes it stronger than witnesses who watched the money change hands?

shevuot/45.question: If a man is believed because he could have denied everything, is that real credibility, or only a reward for telling part of the truth?

shevuot/49.question: Why should the false oath a man volunteers count against him, while the same false words spoken because the judges demanded them do not?

avodah-zarah/2.question: If the Jews accepted the Torah only with a mountain suspended over them, what does their acceptance prove that the refusal of the nations does not?

avodah-zarah/8.question: Once the twelve months have passed and the feast is permitted, is a guest answerable for what he eats there or for what his presence does to his host?

avodah-zarah/9.question: If redemption was close enough in year 400 that a field offered for one dinar was a bad purchase, what is someone buying land to make of that advice once year 400 is long past?

avodah-zarah/11.question: If the fire is only evidence that a king mattered enough for idol worship to follow, is a day closed to business by what the mourners actually did or by how much they cared?

avodah-zarah/13.question: If paying a gentile for his animal counts as reducing his possessions, when does a purchase ever count as enriching the seller?

avodah-zarah/14.question: If a man who accepts a black rooster instead might still be pretending, is there anything a buyer could do that would count as proof of what he intends?

avodah-zarah/15.question: If a buyer gets the benefit of the doubt when he might work the cow, why does a man already suspected of reselling get none?

avodah-zarah/21.question: If the Sages forbid selling fields even far from Eretz Yisrael because a distant sale might lead to a sale inside it, why does Abaye's limit on harm two steps away not excuse that distant seller too?

avodah-zarah/23.question: If desire overcomes a man's interest in money when an animal is at hand, why is a captor's fear of losing the ransom trusted to keep a woman safe?

avodah-zarah/25.question: If the model for staying safe on the road is Jacob naming Seir and going to Succoth, is that a lie the danger excuses, or a promise to Esau that Jacob simply broke?

avodah-zarah/30.question: If the reasoning about snakes was good enough to be accepted as an explanation, why should a risk of death be the one place where good reasoning is not allowed to decide?

avodah-zarah/31.question: If what actually keeps the wine untouched is the seller's fear of being seen by a crowd, is a seal a barrier at all, or only a mark that would show someone had been there?

avodah-zarah/33.question: If a coating is smooth enough to keep a gentile's wine out of the jug, why is it still an open question whether it keeps leaven out, or is absorption measured separately for each prohibition?

avodah-zarah/38.question: If singeing leaves the cooked ear permitted because the gentile was not trying to cook, and turning meat over leaves it permitted because a Jew had a hand in it, what is the decree guarding against: the gentile's work on the food or his intention toward it?

avodah-zarah/40.question: When two courts announce opposite rulings about the same boat of fish, and a later sage refuses to decide either way, what makes either announcement binding on a buyer?

avodah-zarah/43.question: If a figure of the moon may not be made, yet may be made when the purpose is study and teaching, does the ban attach to the image or to what the maker intends by it?

avodah-zarah/49.question: If throwing coins worth the wood into the water releases the loaves, was the thing forbidden the benefit a person gained, which can be priced, or the bread itself, which no payment reaches?

avodah-zarah/54.question: If the world follows its course and judgment is left for later, why is God described as forced to give life to the child of adultery against his own will?

avodah-zarah/55.question: If the suffering departs on the appointed day precisely so as not to break its oath, is heaven acting honestly when that same faithfulness is what convinces the man the idol healed him?

avodah-zarah/56.question: If a gentile's hands must be tied to keep the wine permitted, why does his foot in the same winepress not count as an act of worship?

avodah-zarah/57.question: When two courts proclaim opposite rulings about the same barrel, does a ruling become the law by being announced, or only by being right?

avodah-zarah/59.question: If Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba already knew enough to report all three practices, what was he waiting for while he stood in Gavla saying nothing?

avodah-zarah/60.question: If the man who climbs out alive forbids the wine by his gratitude and the man who climbs out dead does not, is the wine judged by the touch itself or by an intention nobody can see?

avodah-zarah/63.question: Does saying that an animal belongs to God take it out of a person's hands as completely as giving it away, when the animal is still standing there?

avodah-zarah/64.question: If the only thing separating permitted coins from forbidden ones is what the creditor privately hoped for, can a wish ever be measured closely enough to decide whether money is clean?

avodah-zarah/67.question: If the same vinegar can forbid a dish for the good it did at first and permit it for the harm it does now, which moment decides what a thing is?

avodah-zarah/68.question: If Rava cannot say why Rav forbade the beer, can a ruling still be relied on once nobody knows the reason behind it?

avodah-zarah/72.question: If Rava can forbid the wine still sitting in the barrel because all of it is moving toward the gentile's hand, why does a stream of wine falling out of a funnel not count as the same kind of contact?

avodah-zarah/75.question: If a pot that has never touched food must be immersed while a borrowed one need not, is the water removing something from the pot or marking that it changed hands?

horayot/2.question: When does deferring to a court you are sure is mistaken stop being obedience and start being your own error?

horayot/4.question: If the crudest error frees the court from the bull because it counts as ignorance rather than a ruling, is a body least answerable for its decisions exactly when it is most wrong?

horayot/6.question: If the men who worshipped idols in Zedekiah's day were dead, is a congregation that never dies atoning for their sin or for its own?

horayot/7.question: If the priest's mistake and the court's mistake come from different verses but end in the same offering, is a sin counted by its source or by its remedy?
