horayot/8.question: Why should each kind of sinner need an animal of its own, so that a whole city could end up owing an offering with no animal left for it?

horayot/9.question: If the High Priest's wealth has to be handed to him by his fellow priests, in what sense was he ever a man who cannot become poor?

horayot/10.question: If Lot's daughters are counted righteous because they believed the world had been destroyed, can a sincere mistake about the world make the act itself right?

zevachim/2.question: If an animal over which nothing was said counts as slaughtered for its own purpose, why does saying the wrong purpose out loud cost the owner the obligation he came to discharge?

zevachim/3.question: If an animal slaughtered with no particular intention is still fit, why does a bill of divorce with nothing specified fail?

zevachim/4.question: If the four rites are one continuous handling of a single animal, why should one stringency in one rite be enough to block learning a requirement from it to the rest?

zevachim/5.question: If a mother's burnt offering can atone for sins beyond the one it was brought for, why should her death stop it from covering her heirs' own failings?

zevachim/6.question: If the verse already forgives the sins that no offering covers, why must the second goat's consecration be timed to the knife so that it covers them?

zevachim/7.question: If the pardon is granted before the animal ever reaches the altar, what does appeasing the king add to already being forgiven by him?

zevachim/9.question: The tithe and the firstborn are each ruled out by a verse, but the thanks offering only by the claim that such a result would be odd, so can an argument from what seems implausible settle a case as firmly as a verse?

zevachim/10.question: If every comparison between a sin offering and a guilt offering can be refuted by naming some difference, does a verse joining them prove they share the rule, or only declare that they do?

zevachim/13.question: If Tarfon can recognize the lost teaching but still cannot say it himself, does his oath add anything to what Akiva worked out on his own?

zevachim/15.question: The page concludes that blood carried the wrong way can be carried again properly, so what would make a mistake in the middle of a rite final rather than repairable?

zevachim/17.question: If the word "pure" in one verse can mean no more than pure enough for this single rite, what stops a reader from reading every demand for purity down to its own minimum?

zevachim/18.question: If extra cloth always counts as present, what does it mean that one verse can make a fifth corner immaterial for fringes while the same surplus on a priest's robe still ruins his service?

zevachim/19.question: Why should boxes of scripture worn on the body as a commandment count as separation, when a live louse wandering over the skin might not?

zevachim/20.question: If distraction is what cancels the washing, why should it be measured by whether the priest's body has left the courtyard rather than by whether he is still attending to the service?

zevachim/25.question: Can a vessel be said to receive what falls through the air above it once it has lost the ability to hold anything, or does receiving depend on what the vessel can still do?

zevachim/27.question: The page says the difference is that one flaw happened in the course of the service, but why should a mistake made inside the sacred work bind the altar to the offering rather than spoil it further?

zevachim/29.question: If a silent plan can already spoil a real animal, can it still be called a case where nothing was done?

zevachim/30.question: If leaving a case out of the wording is supposed to tell a student the ruling, how is that student to tell an omission that teaches from an omission that is simply a gap?

zevachim/33.question: If a small opening in the wall would let the leper reach his hands in, what makes the Temple's written plan something no one may adjust even to let a required act be done properly?

zevachim/34.question: If blood is disqualified only when nothing can set it right, is a thing ruined by what was done to it or by what still remains possible?

zevachim/35.question: If the priests may wade in the blood only while hauling wood, and never while performing a rite, is a show of devotion still devotion once it has been kept out of the service itself?

zevachim/36.question: If a plan only counts when it aims at meat that will eventually be permitted to eat, why should planning for people who may never eat it ruin the offering?

zevachim/37.question: If one corner can be enough because a letter is missing from a written word, what makes spelling a reliable way to decide what a priest must do?

zevachim/38.question: If a verse could abolish the requirement of the four corners, and only the count of three phrases rather than four blocks the rival reading, does that requirement rest on anything besides how many times a phrase appears?

zevachim/39.question: If the seven sprinklings count as indispensable only because they are indispensable in every other case, what does the repeated verse add?

zevachim/42.question: If silence during the later sprinklings counts as carrying the first intention forward, what would ever mark the moment a person stopped intending it?

zevachim/43.question: If flour must already be burning before its disqualification lifts, is that release something the flour has gained, or only the altar keeping hold of what it has taken?

zevachim/44.question: Why should an offering that nothing else renders permitted be safe from the priest's intention, when that same intention spoils a peace offering?

zevachim/46.question: If having nothing in mind leaves the offering valid, what does the demand for six intentions actually ask of the person doing the slaughtering?

zevachim/47.question: If the verse demands awareness from the one who slaughters an offering, why should one person's thought ever decide what another person's act amounts to?

zevachim/48.question: If the only thing left for the word "it" is a rule reached by implication, why not let the word be repetition and teach nothing new?

zevachim/51.question: If a verse already settles that these disqualified offerings stay on the altar, what is gained by arguing the same result out through comparisons the Gemara admits do not hold?

zevachim/56.question: If the baraita settles that the meat counts as rejected the moment the second day ends, what is it during the night that follows, when it may neither be eaten nor burned?

zevachim/59.question: If Rav taught the rule for years without being able to name the verse, did the rule depend on the verse, or on the teaching he had received?

zevachim/60.question: Once the altar is broken, is the food left uneaten because the altar is what made eating it possible, or only because a verse ties the eating to an altar that is now missing?

zevachim/61.question: Does permission to eat sacrificial meat depend on an altar standing at that moment, or on being in a place where an altar belongs?

zevachim/64.question: If a single passive verb decides where the blood goes, why does the page still lay out the comparison with animal offerings that pointed the other way?

zevachim/65.question: If reasoning from one offering to another is overturned twice by a verse, why does the baraita set that reasoning out at all?

zevachim/67.question: If the priest's hands can turn one woman's burnt offering into a sin offering, but not when two women's birds are confused, does an offering's identity come from what is done to it or from whose debt it pays?

zevachim/68.question: If a non-priest's thumbnail leaves the meat harmless but a priest's knife makes a swallower impure, is an offering spoiled by the wrong person or by the wrong act?

zevachim/70.question: If pinching the nape keeps a chicken pure even though that bird could never be brought as an offering, does purity depend on how the animal was killed or on what it was fit for?

zevachim/71.question: If a forbidden animal is normally cancelled by the majority around it, why does counting stop mattering once that animal is one nobody may benefit from?

zevachim/74.question: If one fig falling into a pile was enough to forbid all of it, is the pile permitted again by what actually happened when a fig fell out, or only by what onlookers can see happen?

zevachim/75.question: If the same animal may be weighed out once the Temple's upkeep fund holds a claim on it, why should degradation depend on who holds the claim rather than on the animal being consecrated at all?

zevachim/76.question: If the rules protect sacred food only when a mixture can still be undone, is the protection about the food's holiness or about what can be salvaged?

zevachim/77.question: If a blemish nobody can pick out of a pile of limbs no longer disqualifies the animal, is an offering ruled out by the defect itself or only by the defect being visible?

zevachim/81.question: If the Rabbis would have the whole mixture poured into the drain, why does a priest who went ahead and placed it above the line without asking get credit for that placement?

zevachim/82.question: When the comparison between the two mistakes points one way and a single word of a verse points the other, is that word a reason or only a decision?

zevachim/83.question: If both went up unfit, why should the altar keep the item whose missing step lay outside it and send down the one whose missing step lay in itself?

zevachim/84.question: If the altar holds on only to flaws that arose during the service, why does Rabbi Akiva let a blemish the animal already had stay on the fire?

zevachim/86.question: If no hour is fixed for clearing the ashes, why does midnight still decide whether a half-burned limb goes back on the altar?

zevachim/87.question: If the hour of midnight is enough to call the limbs burned wherever they lie, why should fatty limbs, which the fat keeps from burning through, be judged by what the fire has actually done?

zevachim/89.question: If every ranking can be argued the other way, what decides which feature makes one offering more important than another, when the only answer given is that it does?

zevachim/92.question: When one verse can be read to include or to exclude the bird sin offering, should a tally of shared traits with animal offerings settle the matter, or does counting only dress up a choice made on other grounds?

zevachim/93.question: If the same quantity of blood is fit when gathered at once and unfit when gathered twice, is fitness a fact about the blood or about the way the priest handled it?

zevachim/94.question: If Rava could revise his reasoning about leather again and again inside the argument, why does a wrong ruling already taught to the public require an interpreter and a spoken admission of error?

zevachim/95.question: If urine is too unfit to enter the Temple at all, how does absorbing it into a mouthful of tasteless saliva make it fit?

zevachim/96.question: If a conflicting source only leaves two sources standing against each other, is an answer quoted from a mishna any more likely to be true than one reasoned out, or only harder to defeat?

zevachim/97.question: If daily use keeps the pot fit instead of washing it, has the old taste of yesterday's meat been removed, or only put off?

zevachim/98.question: If a stain blocks the water only when the person minds it, can two stains he never minds add up to one that blocks?

zevachim/101.question: If the law came to light only when Aaron argued for it, in what sense was it ever Moses's to forget?

zevachim/106.question: If the Torah already says a man is cut off from his people for slaughtering outside, why must a separate ban be stated in words before he can be punished for it?

zevachim/107.question: If the place of the cut is what decides the matter, why should a man be liable to karet when the animal's body lies outside the courtyard and only its neck, where the knife works, is inside?

zevachim/109.question: If the daily amount of incense was fixed by the Sages and not the Torah, can that amount decide whether a man who burns incense outside the courtyard has done the forbidden act at all?

zevachim/113.question: If Rabbi Yohanan says the land holds no hidden graves and then allows that the red heifer alone is held to a stricter standard, what is a precaution protecting against once the law says there is nothing there?

zevachim/114.question: If the same animal carries karet only when the man slaughtering it means it as another offering, does an animal's fitness belong to the animal or to what the slaughterer intends?

zevachim/115.question: Does a silence earn anything on its own, or only when the one who is silent had something to say and held it back?

menachot/4.question: If an offering that fails to permit anything is disqualified while one that fails to atone still stands, is an act being judged by what it accomplishes or only by what it was meant to be?

menachot/5.question: If the morning light of the sixteenth already permits the new grain to be eaten, what is the omer still doing when it is brought later that day?

menachot/7.question: When a handful could be governed by the meal offering it was taken from or by the blood of an offering, what makes one comparison the right one and not the other?

menachot/10.question: If the repeated words about the healed man's right thumb and toe teach nothing about his own purification, can words written into one case mean nothing there and everything somewhere else?

menachot/14.question: If the priest's own intent can make the two loaves separate bodies, why can impurity striking one loaf not leave the other a separate body too?

menachot/18.question: If the ruling Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua gave five times never changed, what did he think was inaccurate about it before he named the opinion he rejects?

menachot/21.question: If the two comparisons pull in opposite directions and a verse settles the matter anyway, what was the weighing of comparisons supposed to decide?

menachot/22.question: Does a thing become fit for the altar because the public paid for it, or because no person ever put it to use first?

menachot/24.question: If the priest's intention can decide that his handful permits only one tenth's worth of flour, why can it not also decide which of the remaining halves that handful permits?

menachot/25.question: Why should a prohibition's being lifted in one situation make breaking it in another situation acceptable, rather than less excusable?

menachot/27.question: If taking the four species unbound already counts as performing the commanded act, what does binding them add, and can beauty be owed when it is not required?

menachot/30.question: If none of the words themselves are different, can a difference in how Moses took them down really make those verses a separate thing from the rest of the scroll?

menachot/33.question: If the reason for pushing the mezuza out toward the street is that it shields the house, does it matter whether anyone entering ever notices it?

menachot/34.question: If both comparisons were available, why should writing done once at the entry to the land count for less than writing repeated in every generation?

menachot/36.question: If Rav Ashi held that night was a fit time for phylacteries, why give Ravina a reason he did not believe instead of teaching what he actually held?

menachot/39.question: If Rav counts fringes fit when nearly all of their length is winding, what changes when the last loose strings disappear, and why does he say it as a remark about beauty?

menachot/41.question: If cloth lying unused in a box needs fringes while a shroud does not, is the obligation attached to the garment itself or to what someone intends to do with it?

menachot/42.question: If the blessing depends on whether the fringes are owed by the cloak or by the man who wears it, when is a commanded act finished: when the object is ready, or when someone actually uses it?

menachot/43.question: If a blind man must attach fringes because other people can see them, whose seeing is the point of fringes, the wearer's own or everyone else's?

menachot/44.question: The page says the beds once arranged in a forbidden way were later arranged in a permitted one, but if the fringes struck him to stop him from this woman, how does she become the reward for being stopped?

menachot/46.question: If the loaves brought without sheep may be eaten by Torah law, is it right to let them spoil so that nobody misremembers the rule a year later?

menachot/48.question: If catching the falling wine in an impure vessel is no sin because that wine was going to be spoiled anyway, why does the priest's deliberate wrong sprinkling stay a sin when two of the four sheep are lost either way?

menachot/50.question: The page says either half could have been chosen, so both count as fit, but if the end of that flour was settled before the priest ever divided it, what does a choice that changed nothing decide?

menachot/51.question: If paying from public funds is what the Torah itself requires, what allowed the court to shift the cost onto the heirs for as long as the money was short?

menachot/52.question: When a verse doubles the flour and says nothing about the oil, is an offering defined by the proportions of its parts or only by whatever the words happen to mention?

menachot/53.question: If ancestry without learning earns a man nothing at Rabbi Perida's gate, why does he console the visitor he kept waiting by saying God gives the credit to the Patriarchs?

menachot/55.question: If the dough leavens only once, why should the number of punishments follow the number of separate acts of the hands rather than the single spoiled result?

menachot/57.question: Once a man's own leavening has already spoiled an offering, does the rule that protected it still bind him the second time?

menachot/58.question: If the log of oil a recovered leper brings is never burned on the altar at all, what makes carrying it up there a violation beyond the word offering attached to it?

menachot/60.question: What would make a feature that two offerings share strong enough to prove that a third offering also requires bringing near?

menachot/61.question: If a priest can wave for anyone, and Rabbi Yosei himself says reasoning gives no ground to keep women out, what is the verse's exclusion still marking once its reason is gone?

menachot/64.question: If the child comes out of the sea alive either way, should the man be punished for catching the fish because of what he intended, or excused because of what his net actually did?

menachot/68.question: When three teachers read one rule and end up eating on three different nights, is the one who waits longest keeping the law or only quieting his own uncertainty?

menachot/70.question: If what counts as eating or as sowing depends on what people ordinarily do, what happens to the grain and the eggs when ordinary habits change?

menachot/71.question: When a list says six and names seven, the Gemara deletes the line that caused the trouble, so what keeps a count from becoming permission to remove whatever disagrees?

menachot/72.question: If barley cut by day is accepted just as fully, what is left of night as the proper time beyond calling it dear?

menachot/74.question: If the remainder of a priest's own offering is neither eaten nor burned on the altar, what makes scattering it on the place of the ashes an act of offering rather than simply throwing it away?

menachot/75.question: Why should a measure fixed for breaking an offering at the altar settle which blessing a person says over a dish of bread in an ordinary kitchen?

menachot/79.question: If the wine stays sacred and is burned only because onlookers would draw the wrong lesson, is a thing holy by what it is or by what people watching would think?

menachot/82.question: If a verse can make a comparison immune to objection, what is left of Rabbi Akiva's rule that the possible cannot be learned from the impossible?

menachot/83.question: If the only reason a guilt offering has no sacred fetal sac is that it can never be pregnant, is a rule for pregnant animals really being derived here, or is the tanna's view that an unborn animal gains holiness only at birth doing the deciding?

menachot/86.question: If the Candelabrum's light is for people and not for God, why does the lamp get the costliest oil while the offerings burned on the altar make do with the lower grades?

menachot/88.question: If Rabbi Yirmeya settles how much oil goes back into the lamp by pointing out that no vessel could measure the missing part, can the equipment a place happens to own decide what the law requires?

menachot/89.question: If the Sages could find the Candelabrum's half-log by testing it night after night, why does the thanks offering's half-log have to come either from a verse or from Sinai?

menachot/90.question: If the spilled wine counts as sacred only so that no one concludes consecrated things can be made ordinary again, is its holiness in the wine or in what people might think?

menachot/92.question: If placing hands is the act of the one who gains atonement, can the High Priest's hands on that goat count as the act of everyone else it atones for?

menachot/93.question: If the blood atones anyway and no second animal is owed, what does the blame consist of for a man who skipped the leaning?

menachot/95.question: If the Table keeps the loaves sacred once the courtyard curtains are down, why does the same dismantling disqualify the rest of the sacrificial food?

menachot/99.question: Does learning stay with a person the way loaves stay on a table, so that one chapter in the morning and one at night keeps it there?

menachot/101.question: Why should a duty to redeem, rather than the plain ability to redeem, be what makes a possibility count as something already done?

menachot/105.question: If a spoken condition is allowed from the start only because the leper has no other way to be purified, why should his need excuse shortening the time the meat may be eaten?

menachot/106.question: If the donor cannot say himself which flour pays his vow and leaves that to wherever the priest's hand happens to land, has he designated anything at all?

menachot/107.question: If one mishna can hold both views at once, is a vow settled by what the words are worth or only by the thing the words named?

menachot/108.question: If nobody can say which lamb the man meant, is the animal made holy by what he said or by the assumption others make about how generous he meant to be?

menachot/109.question: If the two tellings differ only in which brother did the tricking, can what a man intended when he built an altar decide whether it serves God or an idol?

menachot/110.question: If study already counts as sacrifice, and a handful of flour counts as much as a bull, does anything at all depend on actually bringing something?

chullin/4.question: If the Samaritans' care with bird slaughter rests on a requirement they took on themselves rather than one written in the Torah, is a practice trustworthy because of where it comes from or because of who keeps it?

chullin/8.question: If a white-hot skewer strikes and burns in the same instant, what besides which one happened a hair sooner could decide which is called the cause?

chullin/9.question: Once both kinds of doubt are judged strictly, is fear of poison a different sort of caution from fear of eating what is forbidden, or the same caution under a harsher name?

chullin/11.question: If a majority is relied on only when looking is forbidden or impossible, is it a claim about what is probably true, or just a rule for what to do when you cannot check?

chullin/12.question: If the chicken is permitted only because whoever slaughtered it was probably an expert, why does it matter that the man sent an agent at all?

chullin/13.question: If a child's handling of the grain counts by Torah law, why should the wish that the handling plainly shows count only by rabbinic law?

chullin/14.question: Does it matter whether something was out of reach when the day began because a person found it repellent or because the law forbade it, if either way it stays out of reach until the day ends?

chullin/16.question: If a man's release of the water makes the first turn of the wheel his own act, what has changed by the second turn that makes the same water no longer his doing?

chullin/17.question: Is a knife disqualified by what its blade is, or by what the person holding it does with it?

chullin/18.question: If the rule about travelers already allowed Rabbi Zeira to eat the meat, why did he defend himself by questioning the man who passed the ruling along, and does a teaching lose force because of who repeated it?

chullin/20.question: If the reason for continuing to cut is separating the head from the body, why should the skin be left out of that cut merely because it plays no part in slaughter?

chullin/21.question: If a still twitching man counts as a corpse once the cut reaches a fixed depth, yet Eli's age explains why less was enough to kill him, is the boundary between living and dead one measure for every body or one that shifts with the body it is drawn on?

chullin/23.question: Can a person keep a promise by bringing something that falls between the two things he named, or does naming two things mean he has ruled out everything else?

chullin/24.question: If the fifty-year limit ended with the wilderness, is a person better retired by a number fixed in advance or by someone's judgment that his voice or his hands have gone?

chullin/26.question: Can something later becoming wine settle what it already was on the day it was bought, or is a liquid only what it looks and tastes like at that moment?

chullin/28.question: When the sources argue to a standstill, is the rule settled by finding the better argument, or by watching what a careful person does with the duck in front of them?

chullin/35.question: If a verse about drinking settles what counts as a wetting liquid, why is the verse telling a person to pour blood out like water read instead as permitting benefit from it?

chullin/45.question: If the boundary can only be handed on in words, and the middle gap is left undecided, what does the man holding the knife do with an animal cut there?

chullin/46.question: When two sages disagree about where the surviving piece of liver must sit, is demanding both places caution, or the invention of a rule that neither of them held?

chullin/48.question: If no fatal injury can be argued from another, how does anyone decide a case of a hole nobody has seen before?

chullin/50.question: If the ruling about the late mourner holds whether or not Rabbi Abba ever said it, what did the man gain by traveling to hear it from him?

chullin/51.question: If what is common settles the ruling even after someone looked and found the rare injury in this very ewe, what is left for looking to decide?

chullin/53.question: The page explains that Rav deferred because the case arose in Shmuel's place; if a prohibition stands only because of whose place it is, were those birds forbidden, or only forbidden there?

chullin/54.question: If the principle already covers any animal that could not live long, can a list the Sages counted stay closed against wounds they never saw?

chullin/61.question: The page calls it received tradition that the peres and the ozniyya each have one kosher sign the other lacks, and that fact appears exactly when the argument would otherwise fail, so what does the argument prove if the information saving it is supplied on demand?

chullin/66.question: If scales alone would have settled which fish may be eaten, what is a word in the Torah that adds no rule, when the only reason offered for it is that the Torah was made abundant?

chullin/73.question: If what protects the foreleg is that it could still be put back, does a thing's status come from what it is now or from what could still be done to it?

chullin/74.question: If the same plowing animal is a full animal when someone mates with it and its mother's meat when someone eats it, is there anything left to say about what it is apart from the use being made of it?

chullin/75.question: If the worry is that people will copy what they see, why is a calf with strange hooves odd enough to be an exception while a five-year-old animal plowing in open view is not?

chullin/76.question: If one injury cannot be measured against another, what could ever settle whether a cut the mishna never mentions leaves an animal fit to eat?

chullin/78.question: If the ban leaves a father free to be slaughtered on the same day as his offspring only because the young do not cling to him, should the rule follow the fact when a father's young do stay with him?

chullin/79.question: Rabbi Abba acts on voice, ears and tail as though the mother alone decides what an animal is, so if the Sages leave paternity unsettled, is looking at an animal enough to know what it is?

chullin/81.question: If no one warned him about idol worship, so the death penalty was never going to be imposed, should that unused punishment still excuse him from the lashes he was warned about?

chullin/86.question: If the cuts made by such a slaughterer are only probably bungled, how can eating the meat be treated as certain enough to bring lashes rather than as a doubt?

chullin/87.question: Once the page settles that the coins pay for the stolen blessing, what makes a blessing something one person can owe another in gold?

chullin/88.question: If the working test is whether plants can grow in a substance, why should a verse that calls gold dust be enough to permit powdered coin, which grows nothing?

chullin/92.question: If the clusters of grapes cannot survive without the leaves, is the worth of the vine in the fruit or in what keeps the fruit alive?

chullin/94.question: If a buyer who hears that meat has fallen in for the soldiers and assumes it is kosher has only deceived himself, why does that same assumption count as the seller's deception when the non-kosher meat is sold with no announcement at all?

chullin/98.question: If sixty is the measure the Sages state, can a son permit a mixture at forty-three because he remembers his father permitting one at forty-five?

chullin/100.question: If the nerve's prohibition takes hold only because it reaches gentiles too, why should that extra reach change anything for someone who already may not eat the camel at all?

chullin/101.question: When a sage's view holds together only after his name is swapped with another's in an older teaching, is it the sage's consistency being rescued or the rule's?

chullin/103.question: Is a person who tastes a full forbidden mouthful but never lets it arrive whole in his stomach eating the forbidden thing, or only enjoying it?

chullin/108.question: If the meat is forbidden in its own right, why does that prohibition reach what surrounds it only when the meat gives something back, rather than simply because of what the meat has become?

chullin/109.question: If the milk in an udder was never milk, does the roasted udder give Yalta the taste of something forbidden, or only show that nothing here was forbidden in the first place?

chullin/111.question: Is food forbidden because blood is in it, or only because someone can taste that it is there?

chullin/112.question: Once the page settles that the loaf is permitted and that Rav Huna simply had a delicate stomach, what is it that his delicacy has satisfied by handing the loaf to the man who serves him?

chullin/115.question: If reasoning from the grain threshed by a muzzled cow would permit selling meat cooked in milk, why should a word shared by two verses count for more than that reasoning?

chullin/116.question: Is a guess that some local authority permitted a practice enough reason to keep quiet, or did Levi's silence at the table become a ruling he never actually made?

chullin/117.question: If one word, "fat," makes the sheep's tail Temple property a person may not use while leaving it permitted to eat, does the name in the verse fix what a thing is, or does each rule decide that for itself?

chullin/119.question: If a single hair counts as a handle only when it sits among many hairs, is a thing judged by what it can do alone or by what it can do with its neighbors?

chullin/120.question: If a carcass melted in the sun stops making a drinker impure once the liquid has rotted, is a thing forbidden because of what it is, or only for as long as someone would still want to consume it?

chullin/124.question: Is refusing to accept a reported teaching, as Rav Naḥman did before the narrower version of it arrived, a way of testing that teaching or only a way of dismissing it?

chullin/127.question: If a dried fig can be detached for impurity and attached for Shabbat at the same moment, is being one thing a fact about the fig or only about the rule asking?

chullin/130.question: If every ruling that says the taker must pay is recast by Rav Ḥisda as piety rather than law, what is left of the difference between what a person owes and what a person ought to do?

chullin/131.question: When nobody can say whether Levites owe the priests these gifts, is it fair that the doubt always settles in favor of whoever is already holding the meat?

chullin/132.question: If the same priest owes nothing in his first weeks as a butcher and owes the gifts once people know him as one, is the obligation set by what he does or by what others take him to be?

chullin/134.question: If doubtful dough goes to the priest only because eating it wrongly is punished, while the doubtful cow stays with its owner, is the priest's share a debt someone owes him or a rule kept only where breaking it is dangerous?

chullin/136.question: If the comparison holds only where no verse blocks it, is the shared word "give" proving anything, or is each rule really coming from its own verse?

chullin/137.question: If Rabbi Yosei's four sheep was accepted because of a tradition he received and not because of the verse he cited, why argue over which verse counts sheep at all?

chullin/141.question: Does sending the mother away serve the bird, who is caught in the end whether her wing is clipped or nets wait beyond the nest, or does it only restrain the hand of the person taking the eggs?

chullin/142.question: If a rotten ladder is enough to explain the boy's death, what is left of Rabbi Ya'akov's claim that the promised reward is paid only in another world?

bekhorot/9.question: If a lamb worth less than the donkey is enough to release it, why should that discount be the reason the donkey is forbidden to use until someone pays it?

bekhorot/10.question: If the neck is broken so that the man who withheld a lamb from a priest loses money in turn, does the priest gain anything by that loss, or is making the owner pay the whole point?

bekhorot/11.question: If a lean lamb worth a ma'a really completes the redemption, why should the man who bothers to ask be told to spend three dinars?

bekhorot/14.question: If the private altar reading holds only because every other candidate was ruled out by some other verse, is that discovering what the verse means or filling the one slot left over?

bekhorot/15.question: Is an animal that can be neither offered nor redeemed nor eaten still holy in any sense, or is its holiness only the list of things forbidden to do with it?

bekhorot/16.question: If a debt the gentile may never collect is enough to keep a lamb out of the priest's hands, why should that claim fade after one or two generations instead of reaching the tenth?

bekhorot/18.question: Is a person presumed to give away part of his own property so that a duty gets carried out, even when he may not owe that duty at all?

bekhorot/22.question: If the water in the brine becomes impure again the moment it meets more water in the pot, was it ever truly nullified, or only outnumbered for a while?

bekhorot/23.question: If a mixture is clean to touch but still defiles anyone who carries it, in what sense did the majority cancel the impurity?

bekhorot/25.question: If the ban on shearing the red heifer is set aside because such heifers are rare, why should rarity count as a reason to permit rather than a reason for extra care?

bekhorot/26.question: If paying a priest with teruma desecrates it, why is the fear that people will tithe the same produce twice reason enough to leave the payer unpenalized?

bekhorot/27.question: If the first piece of ḥalla is burned and a second separated only so the rule is not forgotten, what is being kept alive once the obligation behind it has been emptied out?

bekhorot/29.question: If a fee that cannot change with the verdict is enough to clear Ila of suspicion, why does the verse about learning for free rule out paying a judge on those same terms?

bekhorot/30.question: If withholding one rule keeps a person out of the fellowship entirely, why is asking to accept only handwashing not also a refusal?

bekhorot/31.question: If nothing about a repentant tax collector's own word had changed, what made his resignation believable to the later Sages and not to the earlier ones?

bekhorot/33.question: Once the Rabbis grant that a certain death outweighs the ban on blemishing, what is Rabbi Yehuda still protecting by letting the animal die unblemished?

bekhorot/36.question: If one priest's proven deception is treated as his own and leaves the trust given to other priests untouched, why does the suspicion that priests inflict blemishes stay in force against all of them?

bekhorot/37.question: If disgust wipes out the seller's deduction for a carcass but not for firstborn meat, is the buyer paying for what he swallowed or for what he believed he was eating?

bekhorot/39.question: If a hidden missing kidney keeps an animal off the altar while only a blemish anyone can see permits slaughtering a firstborn outside the Temple, what is left to be done with such an animal?

bekhorot/46.question: The page says the Sages were simply stricter about witnesses to a husband's death, so is recognizing a firstborn really identifying a person, or only crossing a fixed line that a forehead reaches?

bekhorot/48.question: If an obligation that anyone can read in the Torah still counts as an unwritten loan, what makes a claim public enough to bind a person who bought the property?

bekhorot/49.question: If the settled principle that Rav prevails in ritual matters is dropped here with no reason given, what is that principle worth?

bekhorot/51.question: Rabbi Ḥanina says the pacing father never conclusively resolved to hand over the money, but if Rabbi Tarfon intended all along to return the coins, what makes a priest's planned refund different from a father's expected one?

bekhorot/52.question: If the firstborn's extra share can be taken back in the fiftieth year with nothing paid for it, was it ever really his?

bekhorot/57.question: If a dead mother's hide is enough to keep a newborn from counting as an orphan, was the rule ever about the mother, or only about what the mother provides?

bekhorot/59.question: If the counting, and not any actual giving, is what frees the rest of the herd, why should a count that might never have reached ten free anything?

bekhorot/60.question: If the tenth animal becomes sacred on its own no matter what the owner calls it, why should a word spoken by mistake have any power to consecrate a different animal at all?

bekhorot/61.question: If the animal can still be eaten once it develops a blemish, is that a real loss the owner may refuse to accept from his agent, or only an inconvenience he has to live with?

arakhin/4.question: If the sum owed deliberately ignores what a person could fetch, why should a dying man's inability to stand before the priest be what puts him outside the vow altogether?

arakhin/6.question: If what holds the gentile's lamp to its purpose is only his complaint, why is a Jew assumed to have given up any claim over how his gift gets used?

arakhin/8.question: Does an offering brought only in case she owes one settle her obligation, when no priest may eat from it?

arakhin/9.question: If the court may declare a new month without anyone sighting the moon, why does it still limit how many months it stretches or shortens in order to keep people from accusing it?

arakhin/10.question: If Purim gets no song because the rescue left the Jews still serving Ahasuerus, does a deliverance that only half changes who rules deserve no praise at all?

arakhin/15.question: Does saying a thing in front of the person it is about, as Rabbi Yosei did, make the words honest, or only unashamed?

arakhin/16.question: If shaming another person is itself a sin, why is the duty to keep correcting measured by how much abuse the one correcting can absorb?

arakhin/17.question: If one phrase in a verse can be turned either to block a poor man from the cheaper offering or to block a rich man from it, what is actually deciding whether a vow is measured by the one who pays or by the one it is paid for?

arakhin/21.question: If the court can press a man until he says he wants to, why should it matter whether he agrees when the animal is set aside or when it is sacrificed?

arakhin/25.question: If a son keeps the field for his father because he stands in his father's place, why is it so hard to say who stands in a woman's place?

arakhin/27.question: When the soil is so poor that the owner takes his field back for one small coin, does the duty to bid first still hold once the gain it was meant to produce has vanished?

arakhin/30.question: Once a verse insists that the man who sold himself can always be bought back, and at the lower price, what is left of the claim that his own sins should make his release harder?

arakhin/31.question: If coins left in the chamber take the house from a buyer who refused to accept them, why does the same unwilling taking leave a wife still married?

arakhin/34.question: If the same priest may always buy back the field he inherited from his father but loses the field dedicated to him, what makes inheritance a firmer claim than land already sitting in his hands?

temurah/4.question: The page explains the priest's lashes by saying his greater holiness makes his transgressions more severe, but is he then punished for the divorce itself or for being the one man forbidden to undo it?

temurah/6.question: When Abaye's own ruling that judges take back the interest goes against his principle that a transgression is effective, which of the two shows what he actually holds?

temurah/7.question: If a man is flogged because passing over sound animals is disgraceful, is he punished for what his act accomplished or for what it says about him?

temurah/10.question: If an unborn animal is already holy because its mother was consecrated, what does the owner's declaration over it add?

temurah/12.question: When one half of the verse seems to put the ashes in first and the next half puts the water in first, the Gemara decides by noting that elsewhere the enabling ingredient always goes on top; is a habit observed in other cases enough to fix which half of a verse means exactly what it says?

temurah/16.question: When a rule survives but its scope is lost, why should the doubt end with all five animals left to die rather than all five left to graze?

temurah/17.question: If a mistaken word still binds the animal, is the man being lashed for what he meant or for what came out of his mouth?

temurah/18.question: If waiting long enough for a calf's calf to be born proves the owner was building a herd, why does the same delay in the first generation prove nothing?

temurah/20.question: Does an animal's holiness come from the category its mother was put into, or from what the animal itself can do on the altar?

temurah/22.question: If neither the owner nor the shepherd can tell which animal it is, but one person far away would still recognize it, is the animal lost in itself or only lost to them?

temurah/23.question: The page escapes the objection by assigning the bread rule to the opposing view, but what would make a consecrated animal easier to give up than a scrap of flour?

temurah/25.question: If the maidservant case settles that an unborn child is part of its mother, why does the Gemara keep looking for readings in which Rabbi Yoḥanan is right that an unborn animal can hold a status of its own?

temurah/27.question: When a man has already made three forbidden substitutions in the same sentence, does the assumption that people choose the permitted route still cover his fourth animal?

temurah/32.question: If redemption requires a priest to value the animal while it stands before him, has a dead animal's value disappeared, or only the way of measuring it?

temurah/34.question: If burying and burning both destroy a forbidden thing, why should the choice between them decide whether what is left over may be used?

keritot/2.question: The page rules that a single act can owe three sin offerings, so is atonement measured by what a person actually did or by how many separate prohibitions he forgot?

keritot/3.question: If a bent body and twisted lips already count as actions, what is left of the idea that some sins are committed without doing anything at all?

keritot/5.question: If the first voice declared the drops on Aaron's beard as free to anyone as dew on a mountain, why does the benefit Aaron takes from oil sitting on his own body still count as a separate danger of misusing what is consecrated?

keritot/6.question: If making the incense in order to smell it is punished more harshly than actually smelling it, is the offense the wanting or the having?

keritot/7.question: If Yom Kippur atones for a man who has not repented and wants no atonement, does a person have any power to stay outside forgiveness offered to him?

keritot/11.question: Once his offering depends on her flogging because the verse sets the two side by side, is the man's act no longer a wrong, or a wrong that costs him nothing?

keritot/14.question: If what makes a second prohibition take effect is that the new ban reaches other foods, other uses or other people, why should any of that change anything for this man and this one piece of fat?

keritot/15.question: Why does a ruling Rabbi Yehoshua heard from his teachers settle the matter, while the same conclusion he reaches by his own reasoning can be refuted?

keritot/16.question: If Rabbi Akiva turns aside the last proof by saying he is just as unsure about that case, can a doubt be settled by an example the doubter finds equally doubtful?

keritot/17.question: If the eater's own doubt is the same either way, why should his obligation to bring the offering depend on whether an expert could later examine a piece he did not eat?

keritot/19.question: If his hand picks the grapes he first wanted but no longer wants, does an intention he has forgotten still count as his own?

keritot/21.question: If the substance itself is permitted and the only problem is that onlookers might take it for forbidden blood, can how an act appears make the act itself forbidden?

keritot/22.question: If the doubt is the same whether it concerns a trifle or ten thousand dinars, should the cost of settling it decide whether a person pays now or waits to find out?

keritot/23.question: If pangs of conscience are enough to keep the ram holy, is a person bound by what he sincerely believed he owed rather than by what he actually owed?

keritot/24.question: Does a thing stop being yours when you say you no longer want it, or only when you have actually given up hope of keeping it?

keritot/26.question: If the murderer's own knowledge of his crime keeps an unsolved killing out of the category of sins only God knows, why does a person who cannot tell whether he sinned at all count as knowing nothing?

meilah/2.question: If the reason for the rabbinic decree is that people cannot tell a botched offering from a proper one, why should it also bind where nobody could be confused?

meilah/3.question: If the Sages' decree follows what people are likely to do rather than what the animal is, does the sin offering that draws no decree still count as sacred?

meilah/4.question: If bar Kappara already has the question and hands it to his nephew the night before, what is the study hall for?

meilah/5.question: If the Gemara can call one mishna's wording inexact whenever that wording blocks a reading, what keeps Rav Asi's rule that at least one of the two must be exact from being merely convenient?

meilah/6.question: Does the sprinkling act on the offering as one whole thing, or only on the parts that happened to be inside the courtyard when the blood was thrown?

meilah/7.question: If the condition Akiva never stated, that the two animals were slaughtered at the same moment, turns out to be correct, was his answer to his student honest teaching or only lucky?

meilah/8.question: If the blood squeezed out at the altar's base is only whatever happens to be left over, can a step that may have nothing left to do still be the thing that completes the atonement?

meilah/9.question: If the ash has already served every purpose it was set aside for, does the rule that a priest must dress for the job of carrying it away prove the ash is still holy, or only that the carrying is holy work?

meilah/10.question: If a verse settles the matter anyway, does the reasoning that reached the opposite conclusion still count for anything?

meilah/12.question: If blood belongs to the consecrated animal because the animal cannot exist without it, how does that test survive the fact that the animal goes on living after its blood is let?

meilah/13.question: If pigeons that settle in a dovecote only after it was given away never belong to the gift, what makes fruit part of the tree in a way the pigeons never become part of the dovecote?

meilah/16.question: If being named apart in a verse is enough to change how much counts, what stops that reasoning from resetting every other measure, as Rav Adda bar Ahava presses?

meilah/20.question: When someone carrying out your instruction adds something of his own on top of it, does the part you actually asked for stay yours?

meilah/22.question: Can a form of words make two log out of a hundred the priest's portion while nobody yet knows which wine that is, or does holiness need something actual to settle on first?

kinnim/25.question: Why should the woman who said exactly which bird was for which offering owe more replacement birds for the priest's mistake than the woman who left it vague?

tamid/29.question: Once the Temple's wealth is reason enough to make the golden cup an actual cup of gold, what keeps that same wealth from making the three hundred kor of ashes an actual count?

tamid/31.question: If a lamb tied with silk or gold thread is treated with no disrespect at all, why should resembling the way other nations tie their animals be reason enough to forbid it?

tamid/33.question: The page grounds the emptying in a verse, but why should the loudest signal of the whole service call people toward a moment when no one is allowed to stand nearby?

middot/34.question: Does Rabbi Yose's added clause, that the excommunicated man should listen to his colleagues, still comfort him, or does naming his fault turn the blessing into one more rebuke?

middot/35.question: When a building is recorded down to the handbreadth but the purpose of one room has been forgotten, has the place been preserved or only measured?

middot/37.question: Who is the feast for, if the priest sent away in black is still close enough to hear the blessing over Aaron's unblemished seed?

niddah/4.question: If the Sages chose a single twenty-four hours so that no case is treated differently, what is gained by a measure that treats the woman who could not examine herself exactly like the one who simply neglected to?

niddah/5.question: If doubt leaves an object pure because the object cannot be asked anything, why should a person's involvement in causing the doubt be enough to treat the object as able to answer?

niddah/7.question: If the Sages held Rabbi Eliezer's tradition to be correct yet practiced otherwise as long as he was alive, in what sense was his ruling the law during those years?

niddah/12.question: If one husband's pangs of conscience are reason enough to spare a woman the examination, why is the woman with no fixed cycle made to lose her marriage and everything owed her, with pity going to the man?

niddah/16.question: If the blood either was there or was not, why should permission tonight depend on whether they could later discover that they need to atone?

niddah/17.question: If consistency forces the outer stretch to be pure outright, is a rule better for treating both ends of the corridor alike, or for keeping the doubt Rav Huna thought was real?

niddah/20.question: When the experts who know the shades best refuse to rule, is a woman's status decided by anything other than whoever is still willing to look?

niddah/21.question: If blood inside the tissue counts only because that is the ordinary way a woman bleeds, does impurity depend on the state of her body or on the route the blood took out?

niddah/23.question: If a father's grief is what makes a son count as firstborn, why should appearance rather than grief decide whether the mother gave birth at all?

niddah/25.question: If strictness in the face of doubt is already enough to make the woman impure, why does Rabbi Yehoshua reach for Adam's skins at all?

niddah/27.question: If a corpse buried in its cloak leaves dust that never makes a house impure, is impurity something the remains carry in themselves, or only something they carry while they can still be told apart from everything around them?

niddah/28.question: If it is the sages who impose this and not the Torah, why attach the verse about Tamar to the rule at all?

niddah/29.question: Once the Gemara concedes that only most animals discharge those turbid liquids before birth, why is one missing sign enough to weaken a majority rather than just being the exception?

niddah/30.question: If the same dissection is reported as showing forty days by one side and eighty by the other, what would make either report count as better evidence than the verse Rabbi Yishmael reads?

niddah/32.question: How many remembered incidents does it take before a rare thing counts as common enough that every case must be guarded against it?

niddah/36.question: If Rav Asi meant only to obey his dying teacher and misheard the instruction, is the harm done to Sheila bar Avina any less his to answer for?

niddah/38.question: If a conclusion can never be more lenient than the case it came from, what is gained by arguing from the stricter case at all?

niddah/39.question: If those eleven days cannot fix a cycle at all, must she still expect to bleed on her usual day when it falls inside them?

niddah/42.question: Rava had to chase the man down to learn what had actually happened, so does an answer that is true of the rule but wrong about the case in front of you count as an answer at all?

niddah/43.question: If the moment of uprooting decides the matter only when deciding it that way makes someone impure, is that a rule about when a thing begins, or a preference for the stricter outcome dressed as one?

niddah/46.question: If no one is commanded to keep the child away from the food his own vow forbade him, in what sense does the vow still bind him?

niddah/53.question: When the choice between two rulings rests only on which one is gentler, why does Rav Naḥman work to keep Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's words and locate the leniency somewhere else, rather than accept Ravina's swap of the names?

niddah/55.question: If hair and nails are left out because they grow back, is flesh that heals over with a scar really a thing that never renews itself, or is a leftover mark enough to call something unchanged?

niddah/57.question: If Shmuel's requirement that she feel the blood applies only by Torah law, and she is impure in all those cases anyway, what is left for it to decide?

niddah/60.question: When two people are equally under suspicion, should the stain be handed to the one with the least purity left to lose, or does whatever purity she still holds count as entirely hers?

niddah/62.question: If Rabbi Ḥiyya's teaching can be dismissed because Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi left it out, can a student hand on anything his teacher did not already say?

niddah/64.question: Why should a habit counted three times need three failures to undo it, when a habit counted twice is undone the first time it is broken?

niddah/65.question: Rav Ashi blocks the extra stringency by predicting that a man afraid of bleeding mid-act would avoid his wife entirely, so why doesn't that same fear undercut the rule that he separate the moment he finishes?

niddah/68.question: If Akiva's view looks the most correct, why does practice follow Eliezer's, and what is being measured when a view is called most correct?

niddah/72.question: If how often a thing is touched decides whether the decree reaches it, is she being called impure because of her condition or because of her habits?

niddah/73.question: If a single word in the verse can cancel the logical argument, why state the argument at all?
